input.consumptionNotes:
HOW apps/api CONSUMES IT

Add `"@easytree/domain": "workspace:*"` to apps/api/package.json dependencies, next to the existing `"@easytree/config": "workspace:*"` (apps/api/package.json:16). There are no path aliases anywhere in this repo — resolution runs through the pnpm symlink (verified: apps/api/node_modules/@easytree/config -> ../../../../packages/config) into the package's `exports` map, i.e. into dist/. That is why building matters (see build order).

The non-obvious part: **apps/api emits CommonJS, packages/domain is ESM.** apps/api/package.json has no `"type": "module"`, so `module: NodeNext` (tsconfig.base.json:5) resolves to CJS. I built apps/api and read the output — apps/api/dist/config/config.module.js line 11 is literally `const config_1 = require("@easytree/config")`, a `require()` of a `"type": "module"` package. This works via Node's `require(esm)` (default from Node 22.12; CI pins Node 22 via .nvmrc through .github/actions/setup-pnpm). I confirmed it end-to-end in a sandbox: a CJS `require("@easytree/domain")` against the built ESM dist printed the exported names.

The hard constraint that follows: **no top-level await anywhere in packages/domain's reachable module graph.** I proved the failure — adding a single `await Promise.resolve()` to the ESM entry turned the same `require()` into `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`. This would surface only at runtime in the API/worker smokes, never in typecheck. A pure types/invariants package should never want top-level await, but it must be a stated rule, not luck.

Domain code must be imported by apps/api's `domain/` and `application/` layers only; `interface/http` may map to DTOs. Per ADR-001:74-77, domain never imports back toward NestJS/Kysely — the dependency arrow is one-way, and `types: []` in the domain tsconfig enforces half of that at compile time (Node APIs are unavailable inside packages/domain, verified: `process` -> TS2591).

HOW apps/web CONSUMES IT

Add `"@easytree/domain": "workspace:*"` to apps/web/package.json dependencies alongside `"@easytree/ui": "workspace:*"` (apps/web/package.json:16). apps/web overrides resolution to `module: ESNext` / `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` (apps/web/tsconfig.json:6-7), which honors the `exports` map, so the ESM dist is consumed natively by Next 16 — the exact same shape as `import { Button, Card } from "@easytree/ui"` in apps/web/app/page.tsx:1, which already works in the build-web and web-smoke CI jobs.

Two web-side constraints. First, apps/web must import from the package root only (`@easytree/domain`), never a deep path like `@easytree/domain/dist/time-interval.js` — the single `"."` entry in the exports map makes deep paths a resolution error, which is the intended guard. Second, domain must stay free of any Supabase SDK reference: apps/web/test/no-supabase-import.test.ts is a static guard scoped to apps/web, so it would NOT catch a leak that arrives through the domain package. Keeping packages/domain dependency-free is what actually prevents that.

Types cross the boundary, values mostly don't: components should `import type { TimeInterval }` and call `validateInterval` only for optimistic UX feedback. INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md:110 is explicit that client-side conflict logic is never authority — sharing the function is fine precisely because the server re-validates with the same code (:108).

WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME

ADR-001:77 forbids `packages/shared`. `packages/domain` is only compliant while it stays a *domain* package — reject anything that is merely "used by two apps" (HTTP helpers, date formatters for display, logger wrappers, env access). The mechanical guards are: zero `dependencies` in package.json, `types: []` in both tsconfigs, and the S3-02 architecture test (docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md:215, `apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts`). None of those catches a stray React or Kysely import — that needs an explicit eslint `no-restricted-imports` block or an assertion in the architecture test naming packages/domain.
input.buildOrderNotes:
turbo.json needs NO change. Its tasks are global, not per-package (there is no per-package override block in the 16-line file), and Turborepo derives the package graph from the pnpm workspace globs. `build.outputs` is already `["dist/**", ".next/**", "!.next/cache/**"]` (turbo.json:6), which covers packages/domain/dist without edit.

The three consuming tasks already declare the dependency:
  turbo.json:4-6   build      dependsOn ["^build"]
  turbo.json:9-11  typecheck  dependsOn ["^build"]
  turbo.json:12-14 test       dependsOn ["^build"]

So `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` from the repo root each build packages/domain before apps/api and apps/web run — and the CI jobs typecheck, unit-tests, build-web (`--filter @easytree/web... build`, ci.yml:50) and build-api (`--filter @easytree/api... build`, ci.yml:68) inherit that for free. `lint` has no dependsOn (turbo.json:8) and needs none: eslint reads sources, not dist.

WHAT BREAKS WITHOUT A BUILD — measured, not reasoned

I moved packages/config/dist aside and re-ran the real commands (then restored it):

1. Typecheck, `pnpm --filter @easytree/api exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`:
     src/app.module.ts(1,32): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@easytree/config' or its corresponding type declarations.
     src/config/config.module.ts(1,58): error TS2307: ...
     src/main.ts(3,32): error TS2307: ...
   Three errors, exit code 2. Note the error is TS2307 "cannot find module", not a type mismatch — because `types` points at ./dist/index.d.ts, which does not exist. It is indistinguishable from a missing dependency, which is why this is confusing when it hits someone the first time.

2. Runtime, from apps/api:
     ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND | Cannot find module
     '/Users/benjaminpoersch/EasyTree/apps/api/node_modules/@easytree/config/dist/index.js'
     imported from /Users/benjaminpoersch/EasyTree/apps/api
   The symlink resolves fine; the exports target inside it does not exist.

THE GAP TURBO DOES NOT COVER

Any command that invokes a package binary directly instead of going through `turbo run` skips `^build` entirely. The repo does this in two places, both in the mandatory db-gates job:
  ci.yml:123  pnpm --filter @easytree/api exec vitest run test/tenant-isolation.integration.test.ts
  ci.yml:193  pnpm --filter @easytree/api exec vitest run test/tenant-pooling.integration.test.ts
That is exactly why ci.yml:115-116 exists ("Build workspace deps for api tests" -> `pnpm --filter @easytree/config build`). The same applies to the documented local single-file workflow in CLAUDE.md (`pnpm --filter @easytree/api exec vitest run test/health.e2e.test.ts`) — deps must be built by hand there too.

Consequence: the moment apps/api depends on @easytree/domain, ci.yml:116 must become `pnpm --filter "@easytree/api^..." build`, or db-gates fails at the tenant gates with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Verified selector behavior in this repo: `@easytree/api^...` selects dependencies only (resolved to packages/config), `@easytree/api...` selects deps plus the package itself.

ORDERING WITHIN THE PACKAGE

packages/domain's own `test` inherits `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, but it has no workspace dependencies, so nothing is built first — and its tests import `../src/index.js`, not dist. So `pnpm --filter @easytree/domain test` works from a clean checkout with no build at all. Only downstream consumers need the build.

pnpm-workspace.yaml: NO change needed. Lines 1-3 are `packages:` / `- "apps/*"` / `- "packages/*"` — the glob already matches packages/domain. But `pnpm install` MUST be re-run so the node_modules symlinks are created, and the resulting pnpm-lock.yaml (which gains an `importers` entry for packages/domain, plus the apps/api / apps/web dependency edges) MUST be committed. .github/actions/setup-pnpm runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, so an uncommitted lockfile fails every CI job at the setup step, not at a specific check.
pitfalls: ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE (runtime-only, invisible to typecheck): apps/api emits CommonJS and `require()`s the ESM package — verified in apps/api/dist/config/config.module.js line 11, `const config_1 = require("@easytree/config")`. That works via Node's require(esm), which I confirmed against a built ESM dist. But I also proved the failure: inserting one `await Promise.resolve()` at the top level of the ESM entry turned the same require() into `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`. Rule for packages/domain: no top-level await, no async module initialization, anywhere in the graph reachable from src/index.ts. Nothing in CI's typecheck would catch a violation — it would surface only in the API/worker smoke steps (ci.yml:202-227).

ci.yml:116 is hardcoded to @easytree/config. The two fail-closed tenant gates (ci.yml:123 and :193) call `pnpm --filter @easytree/api exec vitest run ...` directly, bypassing turbo and therefore `test.dependsOn: ["^build"]`. If apps/api gains a @easytree/domain dependency and line 116 is not changed to `pnpm --filter "@easytree/api^..." build`, db-gates fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — in a mandatory check, at a step that looks unrelated to the new package.

pnpm-lock.yaml must be committed. packages/* in pnpm-workspace.yaml:3 already matches, so no workspace-file edit is needed — but the lockfile gains an importers entry, and .github/actions/setup-pnpm runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. An uncommitted lockfile fails every job at setup, which reads as "CI is broken" rather than "you forgot the lockfile".

`types: []` deviates from both templates (packages/config/tsconfig.json:5 and packages/ui/tsconfig.json:7 both use ["node"]). It is deliberate and verified — `process.env` inside packages/domain yields TS2591 — but it means anyone who reflexively reaches for `process`, `Buffer`, `setTimeout` or `fetch` gets an error that looks like a missing @types install. The correct response is to move that code to apps/api, never to add @types/node here. Document the reason in the tsconfig or the PR, or the next contributor will "fix" it.

exactOptionalPropertyTypes + noUncheckedIndexedAccess (tsconfig.base.json:9-10) hurt disproportionately in a types-heavy package. `{ note?: string }` cannot be assigned an explicit `undefined`; every `arr[i]` read is `T | undefined`. Model genuine absence with `| null` or a discriminated union rather than optional properties, and write aggregations (capacity.ts) with `for..of` / `Map.get() ?? 0` instead of index loops — otherwise the week-rollover code fills with non-null assertions, which defeats the point.

Framework-freedom is only half-enforced. `types: []` blocks Node globals, and zero `dependencies` blocks zod/pg/Supabase. Nothing yet blocks a `react` or `@nestjs/common` import, because both are resolvable from the workspace root. Close that with an eslint `no-restricted-imports` entry for packages/domain, or extend the S3-02 architecture test (docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md:215) to assert it — otherwise ADR-001:74 stays a review convention and packages/domain drifts into the forbidden packages/shared (ADR-001:77).

No new CI job is needed for this package — but if the S3-02 architecture-boundary CI job is added in the same PR, scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh REQUIRED_CHECKS (lines 31-39) AND docs/runbooks/branch-protection.md (lines 25-33) must be updated in that same PR. The script drift-checks BOTH directions (lines 98-125) and aborts: an unlisted job would become silently optional, and a listed-but-nonexistent check would make every future PR permanently unmergeable — the script's own comment (lines 73-75) calls the second case the more dangerous one.

Vitest 4.1.10's defaultExclude is only ["**/node_modules/**", "**/.git/**"] (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/defaults.9aQKnqFk.js:6) — dist is NOT excluded. Today that is harmless because tsconfig.build.json has `include: ["src"]` and tests live in test/, so nothing testable reaches dist. But a *.test.ts placed under src/ would be compiled into dist/ and vitest would then run the source and the compiled copy — two suites, doubled counts, and a stale copy that keeps passing after a source fix. Either keep the src/test split as an invariant or add the vitest.config.ts with `include: ["test/**/*.test.ts"]`.

The .js extension rule applies to test files too, not just src. packages/config/test/index.test.ts:2 imports "../src/index.js" and packages/ui/test/primitives.test.tsx:4 does the same. Omitting it yields TS2835 at typecheck (verified) even though vitest itself would happily resolve the extensionless path — so the suite passes locally and the `typecheck` CI job fails.

verbatimModuleSyntax stays TRUE here. apps/api/tsconfig.json:8 and tsconfig.build.json:9 override it to false for NestJS decorator metadata; packages/domain must not copy that override. Every type import/re-export needs the `type` modifier or you get TS1484 (verified). Copy the inline form from packages/config/src/index.ts:10-14.

README.md:87-88 and the Architecture block in CLAUDE.md both carry a package inventory that nothing validates. They will silently go stale. Both files are covered by `pnpm format` (prettier --check, printWidth 100 per .prettierrc.json), so the edits must be prettier-clean — but no check will tell you the list is incomplete.

Do not add subpath exports (`./planning`, `./time`) on day one. Both templates ship a single "." entry (packages/config/package.json:8-13, packages/ui/package.json:9-14) and the single barrel is what makes ADR-001:69's "explizite öffentliche Modul-API" reviewable in one file. With `sideEffects: false` the Next.js bundler tree-shakes the barrel anyway, so subpaths buy nothing yet and permanently widen the API surface.

TRADE-OFF, stated explicitly.

Option (b), fold into `unit-tests`: no ruleset change, no admin rights, merge-blocking immediately, zero drift risk in either direction. Cost: the ruleset never names architecture governance, and a red signal is buried inside a 4-package Vitest run. (b) alone under-delivers.

Option (a), own job: named, auditable context in the ruleset; fastest job in the workflow (no build, no Docker), so it is a good partner for `format` in a future negative-proof PR. Cost: the ruleset lives on GitHub and must be re-applied with admin rights.

Is (a) risky in this session? MEASURED, read-only, just now: `gh auth status` → logged in as `DYAI2025`, scopes `gist, read:org, repo, workflow`; `gh api repos/DYAI2025/EasyTree` → `admin: true`. So the ruleset re-apply IS executable from this machine — but I did not run it, and must not: CLAUDE.md forbids production/config changes without explicit permission, and the runbook (:92-93) says cloud agents and CI runners neither have nor should get these rights. Also measured read-only: ruleset 19718704 currently requires exactly the 9 existing contexts; `architecture` is not among them.

The two failure modes are NOT symmetric — the script says so itself at setup-branch-protection.sh:72-75 and the runbook repeats it at :178-182:

- REQUIRED_CHECKS lists a check the ruleset does not contain (PR merged, ruleset not yet re-applied). The job runs and is visible but does not block. SAFE, and detectable read-only without admin: `verify-branch-protection.sh` fails AC3 with "fehlende Pflichtchecks: architecture". That is the correct fail-closed signal, not a bug.
- The ruleset requires a check no PR produces. GitHub waits forever on that context; with `bypass_actors: []` EVERY PR becomes permanently unmergeable until an admin edits or disables the ruleset. Catastrophic.

Therefore the ordering is mandatory: merge the PR first, apply the ruleset second. The script's own Direction-2 drift check makes the catastrophic mode unreachable via the script (it aborts if REQUIRED_CHECKS names something `ci.yml` does not produce) — it is only reachable by hand-editing the ruleset in the UI, or by adding a job-level `name:` (see parserRisk).

```markdown
### 2.1 Die Job-ID ist der Check-Name — was das verbietet

`scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` liest die Jobliste mit einem awk-Parser (Z. 82–93),
der ausschliesslich Zeilen der Form `^  <id>:$` erkennt: **exakt zwei Leerzeichen**
Einrückung, Zeichen aus `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, Doppelpunkt, danach nichts ausser Whitespace.
Daraus folgen vier harte Regeln für jeden neuen Job:

1. **Kein job-level `name:`.** GitHub meldet dann den `name` als Check-Kontext, der Parser
   sieht weiterhin die Job-ID. Die Drift-Prüfung wird in **beiden** Richtungen grün, das
   Ruleset verlangt einen Kontext, den kein Workflow erzeugt — und jeder PR ist dauerhaft
   unmergebar. Der einzige gemessene Fall, in dem die Drift-Prüfung falsch grün ist.
2. **Kein Kommentar hinter der Job-ID** (`  architecture: # EYT-46`): Job unsichtbar.
3. **Keine Kommentarzeile in Spalte 0 innerhalb von `jobs:`**: beendet den `in_jobs`-Zustand,
   alle folgenden Jobs verschwinden aus der Liste.
4. **Keine Anführungszeichen, keine Punkte in der Job-ID** (`"architecture":`, `arch.check:`).

Kommentare **müssen** also eingerückt über dem Job stehen (`  # …`), wie bei `web-smoke`.
Die Fälle 2–4 sind fail-closed, solange der Job in `REQUIRED_CHECKS` steht — Richtung 2 bricht
ab. Steht er dort nicht, greift Richtung 1 nicht: ein für den Parser unsichtbarer Job wird
stillschweigend optional. Fall 1 ist der gefährliche.

The pattern is `/^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[[:space:]]*$/` — exactly two leading spaces, id chars only, colon, then nothing but whitespace. `architecture` (letters only) is well inside that. Hyphens are allowed too, so `arch-check` would also work; the id is what GitHub reports as the check context because no job sets a `name:` (runbook:20-21).

I also ran the five ways this can silently go wrong. Measured outputs:

| Variant                                   | Parser sees                | Consequence |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------- |
| `  architecture: # EYT-46` (trailing cmt) | job MISSING                | fail-closed IF listed in REQUIRED_CHECKS (Direction 2 aborts); otherwise silently optional |
| `   architecture:` (3-space indent)       | job MISSING                | same |
| `  "architecture":` (quoted)              | job MISSING                | same |
| `  arch.check:` (dot in id)               | job MISSING                | same |
| `# comment` in column 0 inside `jobs:`    | ONLY `format lint typecheck` — everything after the comment is lost | Direction 2 aborts loudly (6 checks "not in workflow"); safe but the error message is misleading |

Why not (c) ESLint, despite eslint already running: it cannot satisfy the repo's no-vacuous-pass rule. A flat-config `files` glob that matches zero files is silently green and ESLint has no "this rule must have matched N files" assertion — the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md:164-168 forbids. Worse, `no-restricted-imports` matches the literal specifier string, so it cannot express the cross-module rule: whether `../../workforce/domain/employee` is legal depends on resolving it relative to the importing file AND on which module the importer sits in. `eslint-plugin-boundaries` can express it, but is a new dependency and still vacuity-blind.

Why not (b) dependency-cruiser: capable and correct, but it is a new devDependency with a large transitive tree and its own config DSL, and it still needs a wrapper suite to prove the red case and the non-vacuity assertions — so it buys resolution machinery this repo does not need (measured: zero tsconfig `paths` aliases, and every relative specifier in the tree already resolves with a 12-line candidate resolver). CLAUDE.md's brief says prefer zero new deps; the repo's whole quality surface is eslint + prettier + vitest.

Why (a)+(d) together: a pure hand-written walker would need regexes over source text, which produce false negatives on `export * from`, type-position `import("x")` and multi-line imports, and false positives on commented-out imports. `ts.preProcessFile(text, true, true)` is a public TypeScript API that gives parser-accurate specifier extraction plus source positions for free, from a package already pinned at the root. Measured: it caught all eight import forms in a probe and ignored both a commented-out import and an import-shaped string literal.

Why it must be a Vitest suite rather than a bash script: the repo's evidence culture demands a permanent, executed red case (ADR-001:120 "Architekturtests verhindern verbotene Imports"; ADR-001:106 "Modulgrenzen müssen aktiv getestet werden; NestJS allein genügt nicht"), and Vitest lets the *checker itself* be unit-tested against a synthetic violating tree — the same shape as the repo's existing `apps/api/test/tenant-gate.fail-closed.test.ts`, which spawns a child run to prove the gate. /**
 * Modulkatalog und Tabellenbesitz (EYT-46).
 *
 * ## Was diese Datei ist
 *
 * Die eine eingefrorene Namensliste der Fachmodule. Verzeichnisname, Eintrag in
 * `MODULE_SLUGS` und jeder Typparameter sind derselbe String — genau deshalb
 * existiert die Liste. Sie ist die Nicht-Leerlauf-Bremse des Architekturtests:
 * `SCAFFOLDED_MODULES` verlangt für jedes genannte Modul echte Dateien, statt
 * eine Metrik über zufällig gefundene Dateien zu zählen.
 *
 * ## Was diese Datei NICHT ist
 *
 * **Tabellenbesitz ist zur Laufzeit NICHT erzwungen.** Es gibt in
 * `supabase/migrations/` genau eine Anwendungsrolle (`authenticated`), und die
 * Grants in `20260723222457_0002_tenancy.sql` gelten für alle schreibbaren
 * Tabellen. RLS filtert nach Mandant (`app.user_org_ids()`), nicht nach Modul.
 * Jeder Modulcode kann also innerhalb seines Mandanten jede Tabelle schreiben,
 * und PostgreSQL nimmt das an.
 *
 * ADR-001 Z. 75 („Ein Modul schreibt nur seine eigenen Tabellen") ist damit
 * heute eine **Reviewkonvention plus dieser Registereintrag**, keine Invariante.
 * ADR-001 Z. 78 („Dependency- und Tabellenbesitzregeln werden in CI geprüft")
 * gilt für die Dependency-Hälfte; die Tabellenbesitz-Hälfte ist offen und darf
 * nicht als erfüllt gemeldet werden. Eine echte Durchsetzung bräuchte je Modul
 * eine eigene Datenbankrolle mit eigenen Grants — das gehört zu EYT-86 und ist
 * dort zu entscheiden.
 */

/**
 * Eingefrorene Modul-Slugs.
 *
 * Quelle ist ADR-001 Z. 60 (der bindende Architekturvertrag). Dessen Einträge
 * sind Prosa mit Schrägstrichen und deshalb keine gültigen Verzeichnisnamen;
 * hier stehen die daraus abgeleiteten, eindeutigen Slugs:
 *
 * | ADR-001 Z. 60        | Slug             |
 * | -------------------- | ---------------- |
 * | Tenancy/Identity     | `tenancy`        |
 * | Workforce            | `workforce`      |
 * | Sites/Work           | `worksites`      |
 * | Planning             | `planning`       |
 * | Resources            | `resources`      |
 * | Timekeeping          | `timekeeping`    |
 * | Communications       | `communications` |
 * | Weather/Routing      | `weather`        |
 * | Files                | `files`          |
 * | Audit/Integration    | `audit`          |
 *
 * Abweichung zur Analyse: `docs/audit/INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` nennt in der
 * Zielstruktur zusätzlich ein Verzeichnis `absence` und verwendet `time` statt
 * `timekeeping` sowie `notifications` statt `communications`. ADR-001 ist der
 * bindende Vertrag und gewinnt; `absence` wird NICHT vorsorglich angelegt,
 * sondern von dem Ticket entschieden, das Abwesenheiten modelliert (EYT-86
 * führt `AbsenceRequest`/`AbsenceDecision`).
 */
export const MODULE_SLUGS = [
  "tenancy",
  "workforce",
  "worksites",
  "planning",
  "resources",
  "timekeeping",
  "communications",
  "weather",
  "files",
  "audit",
] as const;

export type ModuleSlug = (typeof MODULE_SLUGS)[number];

/**
 * Module, die HEUTE Code besitzen und deren Grenzen der Architekturtest deshalb
 * tatsächlich prüfen kann.
 *
 * Bewusst kurz: leere Modulverzeichnisse sind keine Grenzen, sondern
 * Scheinkapselung mit grünem Haken — ADR-001 Z. 33 benennt genau diese Gefahr.
 * Ein Modul wird hier eingetragen, wenn das Ticket es braucht, das seinen Code
 * schreibt. Der Eintrag ist eine Zusage: der Test verlangt danach echte Dateien
 * in `domain/` und `application/` sowie eine `index.ts`.
 */
export const SCAFFOLDED_MODULES = ["workforce", "worksites", "planning"] as const satisfies
  readonly ModuleSlug[];

/** Schichten je Modul. Reihenfolge = erlaubte Importrichtung (aussen darf nach innen). */
export const MODULE_LAYERS = ["domain", "application", "infrastructure", "interface"] as const;

export type ModuleLayer = (typeof MODULE_LAYERS)[number];

export interface TableOwnership {
  /** Tabellenname exakt wie in der Migration, inkl. Schema. */
  readonly table: string;
  /** Besitzendes Modul, oder `null` fuer globale/identitaetsnahe Tabellen. */
  readonly owner: ModuleSlug | null;
  /** true => traegt `org_id NOT NULL` (ADR-001 Z. 82, dort `organization_id` genannt). */
  readonly tenantOwned: boolean;
  readonly note: string;
}

/**
 * Tabellen, die HEUTE in `supabase/migrations/` existieren.
 *
 * Vollständig gegen `20260723214800_0001_foundation.sql` und
 * `20260723222457_0002_tenancy.sql` geprüft. Das Fachschema kommt mit EYT-86;
 * bis dahin besitzt kein Fachmodul eine Tabelle — das ist der ehrliche Stand,
 * nicht eine Lücke im Register.
 */
export const TABLE_OWNERSHIP: readonly TableOwnership[] = [
  {
    table: "public.organizations",
    owner: "tenancy",
    tenantOwned: false,
    note: "Ist selbst der Mandant und traegt daher naturgemaess kein org_id.",
  },
  {
    table: "public.users",
    owner: "tenancy",
    tenantOwned: false,
    note: "1:1 auf auth.users, RLS nur self. Zuordnung zur Organisation ausschliesslich ueber memberships.",
  },
  {
    table: "public.memberships",
    owner: "tenancy",
    tenantOwned: true,
    note: "Verbindet User und Organization inkl. Rolle und Aktiv-Flag.",
  },
  {
    table: "public.items",
    owner: null,
    tenantOwned: true,
    note: "Synthetische RLS-Beweistabelle aus 0002_tenancy.sql, kein Fachbestand.",
  },
  {
    table: "public.item_notes",
    owner: null,
    tenantOwned: true,
    note: "Synthetische RLS-Beweistabelle aus 0002_tenancy.sql, kein Fachbestand.",
  },
];

  extracts imports with `ts.preProcessFile` (regex would miss `export *`, dynamic `import()`

  the existing `unit-tests` job — deliberately no new required check, so the ruleset needs no
  admin re-apply. `domain-allowlist` is an **allowlist**: domain code may import only relative
  paths inside its own `domain/` layer plus `@easytree/domain`. A blocklist cannot express

feat(api): EYT-46 domain modules and an enforced architecture boundary

Adds @easytree/domain, three real modules, and a boundary guard that has been
proven red against the real tree — not a convention written down.

## packages/domain

Branded identifier types (OrgId, EmployeeId, WorksiteId, AssignmentId, …) so a
swapped argument is a compile error rather than a wrong assignment in a
published plan version. Zero dependencies and `"types": []`, which means
@nestjs/*, kysely or pg cannot even resolve there — `typecheck` is already the

ADR-001 line 74 ("Domain importiert keine Framework- oder Infrastrukturpakete") is a universal ban. A finite blocklist cannot express it. Measured against `ts.preProcessFile` on the pinned TS 5.9.3, these all pass the obvious patterns:

| `http` | `^node:(http\|https\|net\|dns\|tls)$` |

| `typeorm` | not listed |

ADR-001 line 60 names ten. This PR scaffolds `planning`, `workforce`, `worksites` — the ones the sprint-goal slice (EYT-50) actually consumes. The guard runs inside the existing required `unit-tests` job. A new required check needs `setup-branch-protection.sh` re-applied with admin rights, and with `bypass_actors: []` the ordering is a trap: ruleset first ⇒ GitHub waits forever on a context no workflow produces and **every** PR becomes unmergeable; PR first ⇒ the check is advisory until someone remembers. A guard that scans nothing reports zero violations. Closed four ways:

- scope is **registry-driven** (`SCAFFOLDED_MODULES`), not glob-driven — so it never rewards creating files to lift a counter;

- every relative specifier must resolve (an unresolved one would silently skip every path rule);

input.commentBody:
## Umsetzung: PR #12

https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/pull/12 — **alle neun Pflichtchecks grün**, Run [30222096157](https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/actions/runs/30222096157), Status `MERGEABLE / CLEAN`. Evidenzstufe: **ausgeführter CI-Lauf**.

### Geliefert

- `@easytree/domain` — gebrandete Bezeichnertypen, null Abhängigkeiten, `"types": []`. Dadurch kann dort `@nestjs/*`, `kysely` oder `pg` nicht einmal auflösen: `typecheck` ist die Durchsetzung von ADR-001 Z. 74 auf Paketebene, bevor ein Test überhaupt greift.
- Module `planning`, `workforce`, `worksites` mit echtem Domain- und Application-Inhalt und benennenden `index.ts`.
- Architekturwächter in `apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts` — sechs Regeln plus Stern-Re-Export-Prüfung, Importextraktion über `ts.preProcessFile`.
- Zwei latente Repo-Defekte gefixt (siehe unten).

### Ehrliche Akzeptanzkriterien-Bilanz

| AK | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Benannte Module besitzen Domain-, Application-, Infrastructure- und Interface-Grenzen | **teilweise** — `domain/` und `application/` haben echten Inhalt und werden erzwungen. `infrastructure/` und `interface/http/` kommen mit EYT-45 und EYT-47; die Schichtregel deckt sie ab, sobald sie existieren. |
| Domaincode importiert weder NestJS noch HTTP, Kysely oder Provider-SDKs | **erfüllt** — als Allowlist, Rot-Fall bewiesen |
| Verbotene Querimporte und App-zu-App-Importe scheitern automatisiert in CI | **erfüllt** — je Regel ein bestandener Rot-Fall |
| Jedes Modul besitzt eine explizite öffentliche API und dokumentierten Tabellenbesitz | **teilweise** — öffentliche APIs vorhanden, `export *` wird abgelehnt. **Tabellenbesitz ist dokumentiert, nicht erzwungen:** es gibt genau eine Anwendungsrolle (`authenticated`), die Grants gelten für alle schreibbaren Tabellen, und RLS filtert nach Mandant, nicht nach Modul. ADR-001 Z. 78 gilt nur für die Dependency-Hälfte. |
| Es entsteht kein unspezifisches `shared`-Sammelpaket oder globales Domainmodell | **erfüllt für den Mechanismus** — `shared`/`common`/`utils`/`core`/… werden abgelehnt, nicht nur der Literalname |

Zwei von fünf sind **teilweise**. Deshalb keine fünf grünen Haken.

### Bewusste Planabweichungen

1. **Kein neuer CI-Job.** Der Wächter läuft im bestehenden Pflichtjob `unit-tests`. Ein neuer Pflichtcheck verlangt ein erneutes `setup-branch-protection.sh` mit Adminrechten; bei `bypass_actors: []` macht die falsche Reihenfolge **jeden** PR dauerhaft unmergebar. Gleiche Blockwirkung, ohne dieses Risiko.
2. **Nur drei statt zehn Module.** ADR-001 Z. 60 nennt zehn. Leere Modulordner sind keine Grenzen — ADR-001 Z. 33 nennt „Scheinkapselung ohne Architekturtests" ausdrücklich als Gefahr. Alle zehn Slugs sind in `module-catalogue.ts` eingefroren; jedes weitere wird von dem Ticket gerüstet, das seinen Code schreibt.

### Zwei latente Repo-Defekte, dabei gefunden und gefixt

1. **`ci.yml` baute eine hartkodierte Workspace-Abhängigkeit** (`@easytree/config`) vor den fail-closed Tenant-Gates. `@easytree/domain` als zweite Abhängigkeit von `apps/api` hätte die Gates gegen ein ungebautes `dist/` laufen lassen — sichtbar als Tenant-Gate-Fehler, nicht als veraltete Bauliste. Jetzt `pnpm --filter @easytree/api^... build`. Der grüne `db-gates`-Lauf belegt den Fix.
2. **`verify-branch-protection.sh` führte eine zweite `REQUIRED_CHECKS`-Liste ohne Drift-Prüfung.** `setup-branch-protection.sh` prüft seine Liste beidseitig gegen `ci.yml`, `verify` gar nicht — ein nur in `setup` nachgezogener Job hätte `verify` weiterhin `PASS AC3` über eine veraltete Liste melden lassen. Beidseitige Prüfung ergänzt, Auslösung gegen einen künstlich gedrifteten Workflow bewiesen.

### Zum Entstehungsweg

Der Entwurf wurde vor der Umsetzung adversarisch geprüft und **verworfen** (zwei unabhängige Prüfer, beide `NEEDS_CHANGES`). Erzwungene Änderungen: Blockliste → Allowliste, Geltungsbereich auf ganz `apps/api/src/**`, registergetriebene statt zählergetriebene Nicht-Leerlauf-Prüfung, `typeReferenceDirectives`-Lücke, Alias-Zusicherung, elf Module auf drei gekürzt, Kysely-Typguard gestrichen (wäre `never` gewesen, da kysely noch in keiner package.json steht).

Der anschließende Auto-Review am PR fand vier weitere Fail-Open-Löcher — drei davon im Wächter selbst. Alle vier gefixt, jeder mit Rot-Fall belegt.

export function conflictsWithExisting(
  draft: AssignmentDraft,
  existing: readonly AssignmentDraft[],
): boolean {
  return existing.some(
    (other) =>
      other.id !== draft.id &&
      other.employeeId === draft.employeeId &&
      overlaps(draft.interval, other.interval),
  );
}

git add -A apps packages && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(domain): EYT-73 one validated time interval model, half-open

The prototype's calculateHours added 24 hours whenever end <= start. So
07:00–07:00 counted as a full day, 15:30–07:00 was silently accepted as a night
shift, and missing times became eight hours with no validation error. The
overlap check meanwhile ran on a plain time-of-day axis — a second model that
answered differently from the first. That is FIND-004 (High).

Two structural choices, not extra validation:

- A TimeInterval exists only as the result of createTimeInterval. durationMinutes
  and overlaps accept nothing else. Duration and overlap therefore share one
  model because there is no second one — not because a convention says so.
- UTC instants instead of times of day. The prototype could reinterpret
  15:30–07:00 only because it had no date. Here the caller has already decided
  the calendar day, so end < start can only mean a genuinely inverted interval
  and is rejected. The ambiguity disappears rather than being ruled on.

Half-open [start, end) per INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE: 08:00–12:00 and 12:00–16:00
are adjacent, not overlapping — otherwise every same-day site change would block
publication.

AssignmentDraft now carries `interval: TimeInterval`, so a draft without a
validated interval is not constructible. Mandatory start/end and fail-closed
publish become properties of the type rather than assurances in review text.
conflictsWithExisting reuses `overlaps` instead of comparing bounds again.

33 tests: equal times, millisecond boundaries, midnight, adjacency, containment,
symmetry, the DST gap and the repeated winter hour, plus a fully enumerated
deterministic sweep. No fast-check — that would be a dependency for a package
that deliberately has none.

Not claimed:
- AC6 asks for an API negative test on publish. There is no HTTP API yet. The
  type makes the case unreachable, which is not the same as an executed API
  test; that arrives with EYT-50.
- Whether an interval counts as night work is a calendar question needing the
  IANA zone and local business date from EYT-86, not an interval property.
- No maximum duration: neither PRD nor ADR states one, so any limit here would
  be invented.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

fix(domain): EYT-73 make the interval genuinely unforgeable, close six review findings

The adversarial review disproved this module's central claim. It was right, and
I reproduced every attack against the built package with tsc exit 0, no cast, no
`any`, no ts-ignore:

    const forged: TimeInterval = { ...good, startUtc: later, endUtc: earlier };
    durationMinutes(forged)              // -600
    good.endUtc.setUTCFullYear(1999)     // a detected conflict: true -> false
    Object.isFrozen(good)                // false

Object spread carries symbol-keyed properties, so the brand travelled while the
data did not. And `readonly startUtc: Date` froze the reference, not the Date.
Both were fail-open — the exact failure class the module claims to eliminate.

Rework:

- TimeInterval is now a class with #private fields and a private constructor.
  TypeScript types such classes nominally, so a structurally identical literal
  or spread is rejected: TS2739 "missing #private, startMs, endMs, toJSON".
- State is epoch milliseconds. `startUtc`/`endUtc` are getters returning a fresh
  Date each call, so no outbound alias can break a validated interval, and
  Object.freeze in the constructor stops plain-JS overwrites.
- Object.assign remains a type-level hole — TypeScript types it as an
  intersection, so the result still counts as TimeInterval while lacking the
  private fields at runtime. Closed with an instanceof guard in every consumer:
  a TypeError instead of a silent "no conflict".
- toJSON, because state in #private fields would otherwise serialize to {}. The
  way back deliberately goes through create() rather than a silent revive.

Five further findings, all verified before acting:

- conflictsWithExisting ignored orgId entirely. A same-named employee id in a
  foreign organisation could raise or mask a conflict. Multi-tenancy is
  non-negotiable per CLAUDE.md; the predicate now compares orgId, with a
  cross-tenant test.
- Self-exclusion via `other.id !== draft.id` was fail-open: two unsaved drafts
  carrying the same placeholder id excluded each other from the check, so a real
  overlap went unreported. Replaced by an explicit `excludeId` parameter, with
  the placeholder case as a regression test.
- The doc comment claimed the database secures the same invariant under
  concurrency via EYT-49. There is no assignment table, no EXCLUDE constraint,
  and EYT-49 is open. Rewritten to state plainly that no concurrency protection
  exists yet.
- RESOURCE_DOUBLE_BOOKED was a declared conflict code with no producer —
  AssignmentDraft carries no resource. Removed until FIND-005 is modelled; a
  code with no producer reads as "handled" to every downstream reader.
- The two DST tests were UTC arithmetic identities that would pass on any pair
  of dates the same distance apart. They now assert the Europe/Berlin wall-clock
  rendering via Intl, so they fail if the date is not a real transition.
- hasAnyOverlap's neighbour-only comparison was argued in a comment. Now checked
  against a brute-force O(n^2) oracle over every triple of an enumerated grid.

35 domain tests, 7 planning tests, all eight turbo tasks green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Task S3-03 of the Sprint 3 plan. **Does not close EYT-73** — see the scorecard.

## The bug

The prototype's `calculateHours` added 24 hours whenever `end <= start`. `07:00–07:00` counted as a full day, `15:30–07:00` was silently accepted as a night shift, missing times became eight hours with no validation error. The overlap check meanwhile ran on a plain time-of-day axis — a second model that answered differently from the first. `FIND-004`, High.

## The fix is structural, not more validation

`TimeInterval` is a class with `#private` fields and a private constructor. TypeScript types such classes nominally, so there is no second way to obtain one, and `durationMinutes`/`overlaps` accept nothing else. State is epoch milliseconds; `startUtc`/`endUtc` are getters returning a fresh `Date` each call.

UTC instants replace times of day. The prototype could reinterpret `15:30–07:00` only because it had no date — here the caller has already decided the calendar day, so `end < start` can only mean a genuinely inverted interval.

Half-open `[start, end)` per INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE: `08:00–12:00` and `12:00–16:00` are adjacent, not overlapping. Otherwise every same-day site change would block publication.

## The first draft of this PR was wrong, and the review caught it

I claimed the branded interface made forgery impossible. It did not. Reproduced against the built package with `tsc` exit 0 — no cast, no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`:

| attack | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ ...good, startUtc: later, endUtc: earlier }` | `tsc` clean, `durationMinutes` = **−600** | `TS2739: missing #private, startMs, endMs, toJSON` |
| `Object.assign({}, good, { endUtc: … })` | `overlaps` silently `false` | `TypeError` — fail-closed |
| `good.endUtc.setUTCFullYear(1999)` | detected conflict flipped `true → false` | no effect; `Object.isFrozen` = `true` |
| `JSON.stringify(good)` | `{}` — silent data loss | lossless via `toJSON` |

`Object.assign` stays a *type-level* hole — TypeScript types it as an intersection, so the result still counts as `TimeInterval` while lacking the private fields at runtime. Closed with an `instanceof` guard in every consumer: a loud `TypeError` beats a quiet "no conflict".

## Five further findings, each verified before acting

1. **`conflictsWithExisting` ignored `orgId` entirely.** A matching employee id in a foreign organisation could raise or mask a conflict. Multi-tenancy is non-negotiable per `CLAUDE.md`; the predicate now compares `orgId`, with a cross-tenant test.
2. **Self-exclusion via `other.id !== draft.id` was fail-open.** Two unsaved drafts carrying the same placeholder id excluded each other, so a real overlap went unreported. Replaced by an explicit `excludeId` parameter; the placeholder case is now a regression test.
3. **A doc comment claimed the database secures the same invariant under concurrency via EYT-49.** There is no assignment table, no `EXCLUDE` constraint, and EYT-49 is open. Rewritten to state plainly that **no concurrency protection exists yet**.
4. **`RESOURCE_DOUBLE_BOOKED` was a declared conflict code with no producer** — `AssignmentDraft` carries no resource. Removed until `FIND-005` is modelled. A code with no producer reads as "handled" to every downstream reader.
5. **The two DST tests were decorative.** They asserted UTC arithmetic identities that would pass on any pair of dates the same distance apart. They now assert the Europe/Berlin wall-clock rendering via `Intl`, so they fail if the date is not a real transition. (Verified independently: 2026-03-29 and 2026-10-25 are the actual last Sundays; `00:00Z→02:00Z` renders `01:00→04:00` local — 3 h on the clock, 2 h elapsed.)

Plus: `hasAnyOverlap`'s neighbour-only comparison was argued in a comment. It is now checked against a brute-force O(n²) oracle over every triple of an enumerated grid.

## Honest acceptance-criteria scorecard

| AC | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Start und Ende sind Pflichtwerte für einen veröffentlichbaren Einsatz | **partial** — enforced on the domain type; there is no publishable entity yet |
| `start == end` abgelehnt, nicht als 24 h interpretiert | **met** |
| `end < start` abgelehnt | **met** — with a consequence stated in the module header: an overnight shift across two dates is now freely expressible. The literal AC holds because night work stopped being a special case, not because it is blocked. Whether it is *allowed* needs the IANA zone and local business date from EYT-86. |
| Dauer- und Überlappungsprüfung nutzen dasselbe Modell | **met** — structurally; there is no second model to diverge from |
| Positiv-, Negativ- und Grenztests | **met** — 35 domain tests; the "property tests" are an enumerated deterministic sweep plus a brute-force oracle, not `fast-check` (a dependency for a package that deliberately has none) |
| Publish bleibt bei ungültigen Intervallen fail-closed | **NOT MET** — `grep -rn '@Controller' apps/api/src` returns only `health.controller.ts`. `publishPlan` is an interface declaration with no implementation, route or DTO. The ticket's own Verifikation clause demands an "API-Negativtest für einen Publish-Versuch" and that test is **unexecutable** in this repo state. It arrives with EYT-47/EYT-50. |

**EYT-73 stays open.** Its stated dependencies EYT-49 and EYT-61 are both `Zu erledigen`, and those are exactly where the concurrency-safe DB invariant and the seeded property tests live. The domain slice is done; the ticket is not.

One more thing the review was right about and I cannot fix: the sprint plan's stated acceptance evidence for S3-03 — "Testfälle waren vor dem Fix rot" — cannot be produced. The prototype `calculateHours` is not in this repository; it exists only quoted inside `docs/audit/evidence/`. These tests exercise new code and were never red. The red-case evidence I *can* offer is the forgery table above, where each attack was green before the rework and fails now.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck` 8/8, `pnpm lint` 5/5, `pnpm test` 8/8, prettier clean, `[architecture] files=70 imports=186 violations=0`. Evidence level: **local run** until CI reports.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

input.commentBody:
## Domain-Slice umgesetzt: PR #13 — Ticket bleibt offen

https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/pull/13 — **alle neun Pflichtchecks grün**, Run [30223405047](https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/actions/runs/30223405047), `MERGEABLE / CLEAN`.

### Der Fix

`packages/domain/src/time-interval.ts` — halb-offenes `[start, end)` über UTC-Instants. Drei Schichten, keine davon als absolut verkauft:

1. **Nominal getypt** — Klasse mit `#private`-Feldern. Ein strukturell gleiches Literal oder ein Spread ist nicht zuweisbar.
2. **Im Konstruktor geprüft** — `endMs <= startMs` wirft. Gilt auch aus reinem JavaScript, wo `private` weggelöscht ist.
3. **Beim Konsumenten nachgeprüft** — `instanceof`-Guard in `overlaps`/`durationMs`/`hasAnyOverlap`, weil TypeScript `Object.assign` als Schnittmenge typisiert und die nominale Prüfung dort nicht greift.

`durationMinutes` und `overlaps` nehmen nur `TimeInterval` entgegen — Dauer und Überlappung teilen ein Modell, weil es kein zweites gibt. Genau das war im Prototyp die Ursache: 24-Stunden-Addition gegen Tageszeitachse.

`AssignmentDraft.interval` ist ein `TimeInterval`; ein Entwurf mit unvalidiertem Intervall ist nicht konstruierbar.

### Akzeptanzkriterien — ehrlich

| AK | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Start und Ende sind Pflichtwerte für einen veröffentlichbaren Einsatz | **teilweise** — auf Domainebene erzwungen; einen veröffentlichbaren Einsatz gibt es noch nicht |
| `start == end` abgelehnt, nicht als 24 h interpretiert | **erfüllt** |
| `end < start` abgelehnt | **erfüllt**, mit ausdrücklicher Folge: eine Schicht über Mitternacht ist als aufsteigendes Instantpaar jetzt frei ausdrückbar. Das AK hält, weil Nachtarbeit aufhört ein Sonderfall zu sein — nicht weil sie blockiert wäre. Ob sie *erlaubt* ist, braucht IANA-Zone und lokales Geschäftsdatum aus EYT-86. |
| Dauer- und Überlappungsprüfung nutzen dasselbe Modell | **erfüllt** — strukturell |
| Positiv-, Negativ- und Grenztests | **erfüllt** — 39 Tests; „Property-Tests" sind ein vollständig aufgezählter Sweep plus Brute-Force-Orakel, kein `fast-check` |
| Publish bleibt bei ungültigen Intervallen fail-closed | **NICHT ERFÜLLT** |

### Warum das Ticket offen bleibt

`grep -rn '@Controller' apps/api/src` liefert ausschließlich `health.controller.ts`. `publishPlan` ist eine Portdeklaration ohne Implementierung, Route oder DTO. Der in der Verifikation geforderte **„API-Negativtest für einen Publish-Versuch mit ungültigem Intervall" ist in diesem Repo-Zustand nicht ausführbar** — er kommt mit EYT-47/EYT-50.

Dazu sind die im Ticket genannten Abhängigkeiten **EYT-49 und EYT-61 beide `Zu erledigen`**. Dort liegen die nebenläufigkeitssichere DB-Invariante (Exclusion-Constraint) und die Property-Tests mit reproduzierbaren Seeds — also genau das, worauf AK6 und die Verifikation sich stützen.

### Fünf weitere Defekte, dabei gefunden und behoben

1. **`conflictsWithExisting` ignorierte `orgId` komplett.** Eine passende Mitarbeiter-Id in fremder Organisation konnte einen Konflikt auslösen oder verdecken. Mandantentrennung ist laut `CLAUDE.md` nicht verhandelbar. Jetzt mit Cross-Tenant-Test.
2. **Selbstausschluss über `other.id !== draft.id` war fail-open** — zwei ungespeicherte Entwürfe mit derselben Platzhalter-Id schlossen sich gegenseitig aus, ein echter Konflikt blieb unentdeckt. Ersetzt durch expliziten `excludeId`-Parameter.
3. **Ein Kommentar behauptete eine DB-Absicherung unter Nebenläufigkeit** (EYT-49, Exclusion-Constraint) im Präsens. Es gibt weder Assignment-Tabelle noch Constraint. Umgeschrieben auf den wahren Stand.
4. **`RESOURCE_DOUBLE_BOOKED` war ein Konfliktcode ohne Produzenten** — `AssignmentDraft` trägt keine Ressource. Entfernt, bis `FIND-005` modelliert ist; ein Code ohne Produzent liest sich für jeden Downstream-Leser wie „behandelt".
5. **Die beiden DST-Tests waren dekorativ** — reine UTC-Rechenidentitäten, die an jedem Datumspaar gleicher Distanz durchgelaufen wären. Prüfen jetzt zusätzlich das Europe/Berlin-Wanduhr-Rendering über `Intl`.

Dazu: `hasAnyOverlap` läuft gegen ein Brute-Force-O(n²)-Orakel über alle Tripel eines aufgezählten Rasters, statt sich auf die Begründung im Kommentar zu verlassen.

### Zur Entstehung

Drei adversarische Prüfer haben den ersten Entwurf verworfen. Meine zentrale Behauptung — Branding mache Fälschung unmöglich — war **falsch**, mit grünem `tsc` und ohne Cast widerlegt: Object-Spread trug das Symbol-Brand mit, `readonly` schützte nur die Referenz. Zwei weitere Runden fanden `Object.assign` und die Konstruktor-Erasure. Jede Runde war meine vorherige Formulierung „strukturell unmöglich" zu stark.

### Was nicht nachweisbar ist

Der Sprintplan nennt als Abnahmeevidenz „Testfälle waren vor dem Fix rot". Das lässt sich nicht erzeugen: der Prototyp-`calculateHours` liegt nicht in diesem Repository, nur zitiert unter `docs/audit/evidence/`. Die Tests prüfen neuen Code und waren nie rot. Als Ersatz dient der Fälschungsnachweis im PR — jeder der vier Angriffe war vor dem Umbau grün.

input.summary: EYT-73 domain slice shipped as PR #13 with all nine checks green after three rounds of adversarial review each disproved my previous "structurally impossible" claim — symbol brand survived object spread, Object.assign defeated nominal typing, and the private constructor was erased at runtime; the ticket stays open because AC6's required API negative test is unexecutable with no controller in the repo.

fix(domain): EYT-74 weekly capacity per employee AND week, with a real timezone

The prototype summed every assignment of a person into a single
employeeWeeklyHours map with no grouping by week. Two weeks that were each
within limits added up to an invented overload — blocking exactly the rolling
four-week planning the PRD requires. FIND-003, High.

## The timezone carrier this needed

An assignment is a pair of UTC instants; a week is a calendar concept. The
timezone sits between them, and without it the bucketing is simply wrong:
2026-08-03 00:30–08:30 Europe/Berlin is 2026-08-02T22:30Z–2026-08-03T06:30Z, so
deriving the week from startUtc files a Monday early shift into the previous
week. Before this commit the repository had no timezone handling at all, though
INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE requires "UTC-Instants plus IANA-Zeitzone und lokale
Geschäftsdaten".

packages/domain/src/planning-week.ts adds:

- IanaTimeZone, validated against Intl rather than a hand-kept list that would
  be stale immediately. An unknown zone is rejected instead of silently
  becoming UTC.
- localBusinessDate via formatToParts, because the output of format depends on
  the locale and the parts do not.
- ISO-8601 weeks. Week 1 is the week containing the first Thursday, so the year
  boundary is unambiguous. Every expected value in the tests was computed
  against the rule, not guessed: 2025-12-29 is 2026-W01, 2027-01-01 is 2026-W53.

Three rules are written down rather than left implicit: ISO-8601 weeks; an
assignment belongs to the week of its *start* and is never split across weeks;
and the timezone is an explicit parameter with no default, because an implicit
server or browser zone is the very failure class being fixed.

## Capacity

The key is (employee, week), not (employee). Warning and blocking thresholds are
separate per AC4, and both are nullable — "not activated", not "zero". No
default limit: neither PRD nor ADR states one, and a number invented here would
read as a business decision.

projectWeeks filters the existing aggregate instead of recomputing, which is
what makes AC5 ("the four-week projection uses the same week values as the
weekly view") structurally true rather than a promise.

## Wired, not shelved

validateDraft in the planning module combines interval overlap and weekly
capacity into stable conflict codes, so the warning/blocker distinction is
observable at the module boundary instead of sitting in an unused library.

One design decision came out of a failing test: capacity findings are restricted
to the draft's own week. Reporting a pre-existing overload in a different week
would make every draft in a full four-week plan look conflicted — the same
practical effect as FIND-003, one level up.

75 domain tests, 13 planning tests, all eight turbo tasks green.

Task S3-04 of the Sprint 3 plan. Closes the `FIND-003` half of the prototype's planning logic.

## The bug

The prototype summed every assignment of a person into one `employeeWeeklyHours` map with no grouping by week. Two weeks that were each within limits added up to an invented overload — blocking exactly the rolling four-week planning the PRD requires.

## The timezone carrier this needed

An assignment is a pair of UTC instants. A week is a calendar concept. The timezone sits between them, and without it the bucketing is simply wrong:

```
2026-08-03 00:30–08:30  Europe/Berlin
= 2026-08-02T22:30Z – 2026-08-03T06:30Z
```

Derive the week from `startUtc` and that Monday early shift lands in **2026-W31** — the previous week. Correctly bucketed it is **2026-W32**. Both are asserted in the tests, the wrong one as an explicit counter-check.

Before this PR the repository had **no timezone handling at all**, although `INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` requires "UTC-Instants plus IANA-Zeitzone und lokale Geschäftsdaten".

`packages/domain/src/planning-week.ts`:

- `IanaTimeZone`, validated against `Intl` rather than a hand-kept list that would be stale immediately. An unknown zone is **rejected**, not silently turned into UTC.
- `localBusinessDate` via `formatToParts` — the output of `format` depends on the locale, the parts do not.
- ISO-8601 weeks: week 1 is the week containing the first Thursday, so the year boundary is unambiguous.

## Three rules written down instead of left implicit

1. **ISO-8601 weeks**, Monday start.
2. **An assignment belongs to the week of its *start*** and is never split. That is the usual shift-planning convention and the only one that avoids apportioning duration; writing it down is what guarantees the weekly view and the four-week projection agree.
3. **The timezone is an explicit parameter with no default.** An implicit server or browser zone is the very failure class being fixed.

## Every expected week value was computed, not guessed

| local date | weekday | ISO week |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-12-29 | Monday | **2026**-W01 |
| 2026-01-01 | Thursday | 2026-W01 |
| 2026-01-05 | Monday | 2026-W02 |
| 2026-08-09 | Sunday | 2026-W32 |
| 2026-08-10 | Monday | 2026-W33 |
| 2026-12-31 | Thursday | 2026-W53 |
| 2027-01-01 | Friday | **2026**-W53 |
| 2027-01-04 | Monday | 2027-W01 |

## Capacity

Key is `(employee, week)`, not `(employee)`. Warning and blocking thresholds are separate per AC4 and both nullable — `null` means "not activated", not "zero". **No default limit**: neither PRD nor ADR states one, and a number invented here would read as a business decision.

`projectWeeks` filters the existing aggregate rather than recomputing. That is what makes AC5 — "the four-week projection uses the same week values as the weekly view" — structurally true instead of a promise; the test asserts object identity, not equality.

## Wired, not shelved

The last review found the previous deliverable was "dead code with one internal caller". `validateDraft` in the planning module now combines interval overlap and weekly capacity into stable conflict codes, so the warning/blocker distinction is observable at the module boundary.

One design decision came out of a **failing test I wrote**: capacity findings are restricted to the draft's own week. My first version reported a pre-existing overload in a different week, which would make every draft in a full four-week plan look conflicted — the same practical effect as `FIND-003`, one level up.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Kapazität deterministisch je Mitarbeiter und Planungswoche | **met** — result is sorted and order-independent; asserted |
| Wochen anhand dokumentierter Zeitzone und Wochenregel abgegrenzt | **met** — ISO-8601 + explicit `IanaTimeZone`, both documented in the module header |
| Zwei getrennte Wochen erzeugen keinen gemeinsamen Konflikt | **met** — the `FIND-003` regression: 8×8 h split 32 h/32 h passes a 45 h block limit that the 64 h total would have tripped |
| Aktivierbare Grenzen unterscheiden Warnung und Publish-Blocker | **met** — nullable thresholds, `BLOCKING` beats `WARNING`, a warning alone can never block |
| Vier-Wochen-Projektion nutzt dieselben Wochenwerte | **met** — `projectWeeks` filters the same aggregate; identity asserted |
| Regressionstests decken Wochenwechsel, Jahreswechsel und DST | **met** — Sunday/Monday boundary, 2026-W53 → 2027-W01, and the spring-forward Sunday |

**Caveat on the ticket's dependencies:** EYT-17, EYT-18, EYT-49 and EYT-61 are all still `Zu erledigen`. This PR delivers the domain half. There is still no persistence and no publish path, so nothing enforces these rules on a stored plan yet — that arrives with EYT-86 and EYT-50. Per-organisation timezone configuration also waits for EYT-86; until then the caller passes it explicitly and `EUROPE_BERLIN` is provided for the pilot.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck` 8/8, `pnpm lint` 5/5, `pnpm test` 8/8, prettier clean, `[architecture] files=75 imports=209 violations=0`. Evidence level: **local run** until CI reports.

## Umsetzung: PR #14

https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/pull/14 — **alle neun Pflichtchecks grün**, Run [30224035647](https://github.com/DYAI2025/EasyTree/actions/runs/30224035647), `MERGEABLE / CLEAN`. Evidenzstufe: **ausgeführter CI-Lauf**.

### Der Zeitzonenträger, den dieser Bug voraussetzt

Ein Einsatz ist ein Paar UTC-Instants, eine Woche ein Kalenderbegriff. Dazwischen liegt die Zeitzone — ohne sie ist die Wochenzuordnung schlicht falsch:

```
2026-08-03 00:30–08:30 Europe/Berlin
= 2026-08-02T22:30Z – 2026-08-03T06:30Z
```

Aus `startUtc` abgeleitet ergibt das **2026-W31** — eine Montags-Frühschicht in der Vorwoche. Korrekt ist **2026-W32**. Beide Werte stehen im Test, der falsche als ausdrückliche Gegenprobe.

Vor diesem PR existierte im Repository **keinerlei Zeitzonenbehandlung**, obwohl `INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` „UTC-Instants plus IANA-Zeitzone und lokale Geschäftsdaten" verlangt.

### Drei festgeschriebene Regeln

1. **ISO-8601-Wochen**, Montagsbeginn, Woche 1 enthält den ersten Donnerstag.
2. **Ein Einsatz gehört in die Woche seines Beginns** und wird nie aufgeteilt. Das ist die übliche Schichtplanungskonvention und der Grund, warum Wochenansicht und Vier-Wochen-Projektion nicht auseinanderlaufen können.
3. **Die Zeitzone ist expliziter Parameter ohne Standardwert.** Eine implizite Server- oder Browserzeitzone wäre genau die Fehlerklasse, die hier behoben wird.

Alle Wochenwerte nachgerechnet, nicht geraten: `2025-12-29 → 2026-W01`, `2026-12-31 → 2026-W53`, `2027-01-01 → 2026-W53`, `2027-01-04 → 2027-W01`.

### Akzeptanzkriterien

| AK | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Kapazität deterministisch je Mitarbeiter und Planungswoche | **erfüllt** — Ergebnis sortiert und eingabereihenfolgenunabhängig, beides zugesichert |
| Wochen anhand dokumentierter Zeitzone und Wochenregel abgegrenzt | **erfüllt** — ISO-8601 + `IanaTimeZone`, beides im Modulkopf dokumentiert |
| Zwei getrennte Wochen erzeugen keinen gemeinsamen Überplanungskonflikt | **erfüllt** — Regression: 8 × 8 h aufgeteilt 32 h/32 h passiert eine 45-h-Blockgrenze, die die 64-h-Gesamtsumme gerissen hätte |
| Aktivierbare Grenzen unterscheiden Warnung und Publish-Blocker | **erfüllt auf Domainebene** — `null` = nicht aktiviert, `BLOCKING` schlägt `WARNING`, eine Warnung allein blockiert nie. Die *Wirkung* auf eine echte Veröffentlichung kommt mit EYT-50, weil es noch keinen Publish-Pfad gibt. |
| Vier-Wochen-Projektion nutzt dieselben Wochenwerte | **erfüllt** — `projectWeeks` filtert dasselbe Aggregat; der Test prüft Objektidentität, nicht Gleichheit |
| Regressionstests decken Wochenwechsel, Jahreswechsel und DST | **erfüllt** — Sonntag/Montag-Grenze, 2026-W53 → 2027-W01, Umstellungssonntag 29.03.2026 |

### Nicht als toter Code abgelegt

Der Review am Vorgängerticket hatte kritisiert, das Deliverable sei „dead code with one internal caller". `validateDraft` im Planungsmodul verbindet jetzt Intervallüberschneidung und Wochenkapazität zu stabilen Konfliktcodes — die Warnung/Blocker-Unterscheidung ist an der Modulgrenze beobachtbar.

Eine Entwurfsentscheidung kam aus einem **fehlgeschlagenen eigenen Test**: Kapazitätsbefunde sind auf die Woche des Entwurfs beschränkt. Meine erste Fassung meldete auch Überlastungen fremder Wochen — in einer vollen Vier-Wochen-Planung sähe damit jeder Entwurf konfliktbehaftet aus, dieselbe praktische Wirkung wie `FIND-003` eine Ebene höher.

### Grenzen dieses Stands

- Die Ticket-Abhängigkeiten **EYT-17, EYT-18, EYT-49 und EYT-61 sind alle `Zu erledigen`**. Dieser PR liefert die Domain-Hälfte.
- Es gibt keine Persistenz und keinen Publish-Pfad — nichts erzwingt diese Regeln auf einem gespeicherten Plan. Das kommt mit EYT-86 und EYT-50.
- Die Zeitzone pro Organisation wartet auf EYT-86. Bis dahin übergibt der Aufrufer sie ausdrücklich; `EUROPE_BERLIN` ist für den Pilotbetrieb vorbereitet.
- Kein Standardgrenzwert für die Wochenkapazität: weder PRD noch ADR nennen einen. Eine hier erfundene Zahl würde als fachliche Entscheidung gelesen.

export const meta = {
  name: 'eyt-47-79-design',
  description: 'Design research for EYT-47 + EYT-79: packages/contracts, OpenAPI v1, generated client, gateway ports',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Recherche', detail: '4 parallel investigations into the real repo' },
    { title: 'Adversarial', detail: 'refute the synthesized design' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/Users/benjaminpoersch/EasyTree'

const CONTEXT = `
Investigate the REAL repository at ${REPO}. Read actual files. Every claim must cite file:line.
If you cannot verify something, write "unverified" explicitly. Do not invent file contents.

Read first:
- ${REPO}/CLAUDE.md (conventions, non-negotiable rules, CI)
- ${REPO}/docs/architecture/ADR-001-boilerplate-architecture.md
- ${REPO}/docs/architecture/ADR-002-integration-canonical-repo.md (section 5: packages/contracts)
- ${REPO}/docs/audit/INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md (the gateway interfaces are given VERBATIM there)
- ${REPO}/docs/plans/2026-07-23-boilerplate-architecture.md (TASK-012)
- ${REPO}/packages/domain/src/*.ts (what already exists)

CRITICAL FACT you must build on, verify it yourself:
packages/domain/src/time-interval.ts defines TimeInterval as a CLASS with #private fields and a
private constructor. It cannot be a transport object: JSON.stringify goes through toJSON() and the
way back must go through TimeInterval.create(). Same for the branded identifier types. This is
directly relevant to EYT-47's acceptance criterion "Domainentitäten werden nicht direkt als
Transportobjekte veröffentlicht".

Hard constraints:
- pnpm only. Node 22. TypeScript strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + exactOptionalPropertyTypes +
  verbatimModuleSyntax + module NodeNext. ESM packages need .js extensions on relative imports.
- packages/shared is FORBIDDEN. apps/api transforms with SWC.
- The architecture guard (apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts + test/architecture/rules.ts) will
  police any new package. Read those rules — your design must pass them, and you must say which
  rule applies to packages/contracts.
- New CI jobs are HIGH RISK: scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh drift-checks ci.yml in BOTH
  directions and the ruleset must be re-applied with admin rights. EYT-46 deliberately folded its
  check into the existing required jobs instead. Assume the same constraint here unless you can
  show it is wrong.
- The repo builds offline (no Google Fonts etc.). Any codegen must work in CI without network
  beyond the pnpm install.
- CLAUDE.md: "Tests fail closed. Never add a skip/fallback that can turn a mandatory check green."

EYT-47 acceptance criteria, verbatim from Jira:
- /api/v1 besitzt ein versioniertes OpenAPI-Dokument.
- Fehler-, Pagination- und Idempotency-Schemata sind einheitlich.
- Der Webclient verwendet einen generierten TypeScript-Client statt manueller DTO-Duplizierung.
- API-Drift und ungeprüfte Breaking Changes lassen CI scheitern.
- Domainentitäten werden nicht direkt als Transportobjekte veröffentlicht.

EYT-79 acceptance criteria, verbatim from Jira:
- Beide Rollen-Shells laufen gegen dieselben Gateway-Interfaces.
- Ein Konfigurationswechsel tauscht Mock gegen HTTP ohne Komponentenänderung.
- Import-/Boundary-Test verhindert direkte Mock- oder Supabase-Abhängigkeit in UI-Komponenten.
- Contract-Tests prüfen mindestens Wochenplan, Konfliktvalidierung, Publish, Bestätigung sowie Start/Stop.
- Fehler-, Loading-, Empty- und Stale-Version-Zustände sind über den Port modelliert.
`

phase('Recherche')

const SCHEMA_SPEC = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['approach', 'rationale', 'newDependencies', 'driftCheck', 'risks', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    approach: { type: 'string', enum: ['SPEC_FIRST', 'CODE_FIRST', 'HYBRID'] },
    rationale: { type: 'string', description: 'precise enough to implement from' },
    newDependencies: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['name', 'justification', 'offlineSafe'],
        properties: { name: { type: 'string' }, justification: { type: 'string' }, offlineSafe: { type: 'boolean' } },
      },
    },
    driftCheck: { type: 'string', description: 'exact mechanism, and which EXISTING required job it runs in' },
    risks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SCHEMA_DTO = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['boundaryRule', 'dtoShapes', 'mappingSites', 'errorSchema', 'idempotencySchema', 'paginationSchema', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    boundaryRule: { type: 'string', description: 'how domain types are kept out of transport, enforceably' },
    dtoShapes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'concrete TS shapes for the transport types' },
    mappingSites: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'where domain <-> DTO conversion lives' },
    errorSchema: { type: 'string' },
    idempotencySchema: { type: 'string' },
    paginationSchema: { type: 'string' },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SCHEMA_PORTS = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['planningGateway', 'employeeGateway', 'stateModel', 'mockVsHttp', 'contractTestPlan', 'deviationsFromAudit', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    planningGateway: { type: 'string', description: 'final TS interface, reconciled with the real domain types' },
    employeeGateway: { type: 'string' },
    stateModel: { type: 'string', description: 'how error/loading/empty/stale-version are modelled ON the port' },
    mockVsHttp: { type: 'string', description: 'how one config switch swaps them with zero component change' },
    contractTestPlan: { type: 'string', description: 'one suite run against BOTH implementations' },
    deviationsFromAudit: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'where you must deviate from the verbatim interfaces in INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md and why' },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SCHEMA_SCOPE = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['deliverableNow', 'deferred', 'blockedBy', 'acReachability', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    deliverableNow: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    deferred: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    blockedBy: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    acReachability: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['ticket', 'ac', 'reachable', 'reason'],
        properties: {
          ticket: { type: 'string' },
          ac: { type: 'string' },
          reachable: { type: 'string', enum: ['YES', 'PARTIAL', 'NO'] },
          reason: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const [spec, dto, ports, scope] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

TASK 1: Decide spec-first vs code-first for the OpenAPI document, and design the drift check.

There are currently NO controllers except health (verify: grep -rn '@Controller' apps/api/src) and
@nestjs/swagger is NOT a dependency (verify apps/api/package.json). So code-first would require
building controllers in this ticket.

Evaluate concretely:
- SPEC_FIRST: hand-authored openapi/v1.yaml as source of truth, types generated from it, controllers
  later asserted to conform. What generates the types? openapi-typescript? Is it offline-safe?
- CODE_FIRST: @nestjs/swagger decorators on controllers, spec emitted by a script. Requires
  controllers + DTO classes + class-validator/class-transformer. How many new deps?
- HYBRID.

The boilerplate plan TASK-012 lists steps "contract tests; DTO validation; spec generation; client
generation; breaking-change check; web integration" — read it and say which approach it implies.

Then design the DRIFT CHECK precisely: how does CI fail when the spec and the code disagree, and
how does it fail on an unreviewed breaking change? It must run inside an EXISTING required job
(format/lint/typecheck/unit-tests/build-*), not a new one. Show the exact package.json script and
where it hooks in. State how you would PROVE the check goes red.`,
    { label: 'spec-approach', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_SPEC }),

  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

TASK 2: Design the transport boundary so domain entities are never published directly (EYT-47 AC5).

This is the interesting constraint: TimeInterval is a class with #private fields, branded ids are
nominal strings. Neither can cross the wire.

Deliver:
- The exact rule that keeps domain types out of transport, and how it is ENFORCED rather than
  documented. Consider: can the architecture guard (apps/api/test/architecture/rules.ts — read it)
  express "packages/contracts must not import @easytree/domain"? Would that be right, or does
  contracts legitimately need domain types for the mapping layer? Argue it.
- Concrete TS shapes for the transport DTOs covering: an assignment draft, a planning conflict, a
  plan version, an employee schedule. Times as ISO-8601 strings; say exactly which format and
  whether offsets are allowed.
- Where the domain <-> DTO mapping lives, and why there (not in packages/domain, which must stay
  framework- and dependency-free — verify its package.json has no dependencies).
- A uniform error schema. The repo already has apps/api/src/common/http-exception.filter.ts
  emitting RFC-7807-shaped JSON — read it and make the schema match what is ALREADY emitted, do not
  invent a second error shape.
- A uniform idempotency scheme (header? body field? what is the key space? what does a repeat
  return?) and a uniform pagination scheme. Both must be justified, not copied from a generic blog
  pattern. If the PRD or ADRs say nothing, say so and mark it as a decision to be recorded.`,
    { label: 'dto-boundary', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_DTO }),

  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

TASK 3: Finalize the gateway ports (EYT-79).

docs/audit/INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md gives PlanningGateway and EmployeeGateway VERBATIM in a
TypeScript block. Quote them exactly, then reconcile with what the repo now actually has:
packages/domain exports TimeInterval (class), branded ids, PlanningWeek, CapacityLimit,
CapacityVerdict; apps/api/src/modules/planning exports AssignmentDraft, PlanningConflict,
CONFLICT_CODES, conflictsWithExisting, validateDraft.

Deliver:
- The final interfaces, adjusted where the audit's version cannot work as written. List every
  deviation and justify it. Do NOT silently change a signature.
- How error / loading / empty / stale-version states are modelled ON THE PORT (EYT-79 AC5), not in
  each component. Is a Result union the right shape here, or an exception? Argue it against the
  repo's existing style (packages/domain uses result objects, apps/api uses exceptions + a filter).
- How one configuration switch swaps Mock for HTTP with zero component change (AC2). Where does the
  switch live? Note apps/web/app/providers.tsx is described in CLAUDE.md as the single construction
  site for the ApiClient — read it and fit into that pattern rather than inventing a second one.
- The contract test plan: ONE suite that runs against both implementations and covers Wochenplan,
  Konfliktvalidierung, Publish, Bestätigung, Start/Stop. Where does that suite live so it can see
  both? Which package owns it?
- How the existing static guard apps/web/test/no-supabase-import.test.ts should be extended for
  AC3 (no direct mock or Supabase dependency in UI components). Read that test first — CLAUDE.md
  warns its guard string is assembled from parts on purpose.`,
    { label: 'gateway-ports', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_PORTS }),

  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

TASK 4: Scope honestly. What of EYT-47 and EYT-79 is actually reachable in THIS ticket?

Facts to verify yourself:
- Is there any persistence? (supabase/migrations — which tables exist?)
- Is there any HTTP surface beyond health?
- Do apps/web routes /planung or /einsatz exist?
- What does docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md say S3-05 delivers, and what
  does it explicitly defer to S3-07/S3-12?

Then, for EACH of the ten acceptance criteria listed in the context above, judge reachability
honestly: YES / PARTIAL / NO with a reason grounded in a file path.

Pay particular attention to:
- "Der Webclient verwendet einen generierten TypeScript-Client" — apps/web currently has
  lib/api-client.ts. Read it. Does replacing it break the existing tests
  (apps/web/test/api-client.test.ts)? What must change?
- "Contract-Tests prüfen ... Bestätigung sowie Start/Stop" — Bestätigung and Zeiterfassung have no
  domain model at all yet. Can a contract test for them be anything but a mock talking to itself?
  Say so plainly if not.
- The repo rule "Never claim done on local evidence alone" and the retro rule about grepping
  deliverables for offen|TODO|FIXME.

Recommend a concrete cut: what lands in this PR, what is deferred to which ticket, and what should
be recorded as a blocker.`,
    { label: 'scope-honesty', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_SCOPE }),
])

log(`Recherche fertig. Ansatz: ${spec ? spec.approach : 'FEHLGESCHLAGEN'}`)
log(`Abweichungen vom Audit: ${ports ? ports.deviationsFromAudit.length : 0}`)

phase('Adversarial')

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['fatalFlaws', 'bypass', 'verdict', 'requiredChanges'],
  properties: {
    fatalFlaws: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    bypass: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete scenario where the design is green but broken; empty string if none found' },
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['SOUND', 'NEEDS_CHANGES', 'REJECT'] },
    requiredChanges: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const design = JSON.stringify({ spec, dto, ports, scope }, null, 2)

const [refuteDrift, refuteScope] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

Adversarial reviewer. REFUTE this design. Default to finding it broken. Verify cited paths and line
numbers against the real files — the research agents may have hallucinated.

PROPOSED DESIGN:
${design}

Attack:
1. The drift check. Construct the concrete change that makes the spec and the implementation
   disagree while CI stays green. Consider: generated files committed vs generated in CI, a
   generator that is not run, a check that compares a file to itself, added-but-undocumented
   endpoints, changed semantics with unchanged types, and the case where the generator output
   depends on formatting.
2. The transport boundary. Find the route by which a domain type still reaches the wire, or by
   which an unvalidated wire value becomes a domain type without passing TimeInterval.create.
3. The mock/HTTP switch. Can a component still reach the mock in production? Can the contract suite
   pass against the mock while the HTTP implementation is broken?
4. Do the cited files and line numbers exist? Spot-check at least six.`,
    { label: 'refute:drift-and-boundary', phase: 'Adversarial', schema: VERDICT }),

  () => agent(`${CONTEXT}

Adversarial reviewer focused on SCOPE, DEAD CODE and HONESTY.

PROPOSED DESIGN:
${design}

The last three tickets in this repo were each criticised for shipping something that looked
complete but was not wired to anything. Read the most recent PR bodies for tone
(gh pr view 12 --json body, gh pr view 13 --json body, gh pr view 14 --json body) — the standard
here is an explicit per-AC scorecard with PARTIAL and NOT MET rows where deserved.

Attack:
1. Which part of this design is ceremony? An OpenAPI document describing endpoints that do not
   exist, a generated client with no server, a contract suite where the mock is the only
   implementation — say plainly which of these applies and which does not.
2. EYT-79 AC4 demands contract tests for Bestätigung and Start/Stop. Verify there is no domain
   model for either (grep packages/domain/src and apps/api/src/modules). If a contract test there
   can only be a mock agreeing with itself, say so and demand it be descoped rather than faked.
3. Would this PR create files whose only consumer is their own test? Name them.
4. Is the proposed cut between "now" and "deferred" honest, or does it quietly claim ACs that need
   EYT-50/EYT-86? Produce the corrected per-AC scorecard yourself.`,
    { label: 'refute:scope-ceremony', phase: 'Adversarial', schema: VERDICT }),
])

return { spec, dto, ports, scope, adversarial: { drift: refuteDrift, scope: refuteScope } }

## Entscheidung

**EasyTree-master wird das einzige kanonische Produkt-Repository.** Die beiden Vite-Repositories werden nicht über Netzwerk- oder Repository-Schnittstellen miteinander gekoppelt, sondern als UX-Referenzen und Quellmodule in das Monorepo migriert.

Die passende Naht ist ein **gemeinsamer, versionierter Domain- und API-Vertrag**:

```text
Planer-UI                         Mitarbeiter-UI
(EasyTree-UIUX)                  (EasyTree-App-UI)
       \                              /
        \  typed UI ports/gateways   /
         v                          v
        packages/contracts + packages/domain
                       |
                       v
              NestJS Application API
                       |
             Domain Commands / Queries

**EasyTree-master wird das einzige kanonische Produkt-Repository.** Die beiden Vite-Repositories werden nicht über Netzwerk- oder Repository-Schnittstellen miteinander gekoppelt, sondern als UX-Referenzen und Quellmodule in das Monorepo migriert.
