-- Migration 0003_app_role (EYT-45)
-- Eigene Laufzeitrolle ohne RLS-Umgehung.
-- Schemaquelle: AUSSCHLIESSLICH Migrationen in supabase/migrations/.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Warum diese Migration existiert
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ADR-001 Z. 85: "Normale Runtime-Credentials duerfen RLS nicht umgehen."
--
-- Bis hierher tat die Anwendung genau das. Jede DATABASE_URL im Repository
-- verwendet die Login-Rolle `postgres` (.env.example, .github/workflows/ci.yml),
-- und `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` reicht sie unveraendert an die Laufzeit.
-- `postgres` ist Superuser; Superuser umgehen Row Level Security vollstaendig.
-- Die Policies aus 0002_tenancy.sql waren fuer die Anwendung damit wirkungslos.
-- Die Tenant-Tests beweisen sie nur, weil sie ausdruecklich
-- `set local role authenticated` setzen — die Anwendung tat das nirgends.
--
-- Der Kommentar in 0002_tenancy.sql sagt es bereits selbst: FORCE RLS greift
-- erst, "sobald der Owner kein BYPASSRLS-Attribut traegt".
--
-- Kein TypeScript-Konstrukt kann das beheben. Es braucht eine andere Rolle.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Idempotente Anlage
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rollen sind CLUSTER-weit, nicht datenbankweit. `supabase db reset` baut die
-- Datenbank neu auf, laesst die Rollen aber stehen. Ein nacktes `create role`
-- wuerde deshalb beim ZWEITEN Reset mit "role already exists" scheitern — und
-- genau zwei aufeinanderfolgende Resets sind die Definition of Done fuer
-- Migrationen in diesem Repository (docs/runbooks/database-workflow.md).
--
-- `alter` im else-Zweig ist kein Beiwerk: es korrigiert eine Rolle, die von
-- einem frueheren Lauf mit anderen Attributen zurueckgeblieben ist.
do $$
begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'easytree_app') then
    create role easytree_app
      login
      noinherit
      nosuperuser
      nobypassrls
      nocreatedb
      nocreaterole
      noreplication;
  else
    alter role easytree_app
      login
      noinherit
      nosuperuser
      nobypassrls
      nocreatedb
      nocreaterole
      noreplication;
  end if;
end
$$;

comment on role easytree_app is
  'Laufzeitrolle von API und Worker (EYT-45). NOINHERIT: ohne "set local role authenticated" hat sie KEINE Tabellenrechte. NOBYPASSRLS/NOSUPERUSER: RLS gilt.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- NOINHERIT ist die eigentliche Sicherung
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Mitgliedschaft in `authenticated` allein wuerde die Rechte automatisch
-- vererben — eine Query ohne gesetzten Tenantkontext haette dann trotzdem
-- Tabellenzugriff, und die Kontextsetzung waere eine Konvention.
--
-- Mit NOINHERIT gilt das Gegenteil: `easytree_app` besitzt vor dem expliziten
-- `set local role authenticated` KEINE Rechte auf public.*. Eine Query vor der
-- Kontextsetzung scheitert mit "permission denied", nicht mit stillen
-- Volldaten. Fail-closed auf Datenbankebene statt im Anwendungscode.
grant authenticated to easytree_app;

grant connect on database postgres to easytree_app;

-- Der Startcheck der Anwendung liest die eigenen Rollenattribute. pg_roles ist
-- fuer public lesbar; der Grant steht hier nur zur Dokumentation der Absicht.
grant usage on schema pg_catalog to easytree_app;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Was diese Migration NICHT tut
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Kein Passwort. Ein Passwort in einer Migration liegt in git und ist damit
-- kein Geheimnis mehr (CLAUDE.md: Umgebungsdateien werden nie committet).
-- Die Authentifizierung wird ausserhalb bereitgestellt:
--   lokal/CI  -> `alter role easytree_app password '...'` als eigener Schritt
--   produktiv -> Secret Manager, nie im Repository
--
-- Kein Entzug der Rolle `postgres`. Migrationen, Supabase-interne Jobs und die
-- pgTAP-Suite brauchen sie weiterhin. Diese Migration aendert, womit die
-- ANWENDUNG verbindet, nicht womit das Werkzeug verbindet.

# wird. Dort gehoert es hin: Readiness beschreibt einen LAUFENDEN Prozess,
# dessen Abhaengigkeit ausfaellt, nicht einen Prozess, der nie starten durfte.
#
# Erwartet dieselbe strikte Test-Preset-Umgebung wie smoke-api.sh.
set -euo pipefail

if node apps/api/dist/main.js >/tmp/role-gate.log 2>&1; then
  echo "::error::API ist gestartet, obwohl die Datenbankrolle nicht pruefbar war."
  cat /tmp/role-gate.log

fi

grep -o "Die Datenbankrolle.*" /tmp/role-gate.log | head -1 || true

cd /Users/benjaminpoersch/EasyTree
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(api)!: EYT-45 stop running the application as a database superuser

The adversarial review of the EYT-45 design found a standing security defect
that predates the ticket, and it is the reason this PR looks the way it does.

## The defect

ADR-001 line 85: "Normale Runtime-Credentials dürfen RLS nicht umgehen."

Every DATABASE_URL in the repository used the postgres login role — .env.example
line 10, ci.yml lines 213, 222 and 230 — and app.module.ts handed it straight to
the runtime. postgres is a superuser, and superusers bypass Row Level Security
entirely. Every policy in 0002_tenancy.sql was therefore ineffective for the
application. The tenant tests only prove them because they explicitly issue
`set local role authenticated`; nothing in src/ did.

0002_tenancy.sql says so itself: FORCE RLS bites "sobald der Owner kein
BYPASSRLS-Attribut traegt". Verified: grep for rolbypassrls / session_user /
current_user / set local role across apps/api/src, packages and scripts returns
nothing. No TypeScript construct can fix this.

## Migration 0003_app_role

Creates easytree_app: login, nosuperuser, nobypassrls, and NOINHERIT.

NOINHERIT is the actual safeguard, not a detail. With inheritance the role would
hold authenticated's table rights immediately, so a query issued before the
tenant context was set would still see data and the context would be a
convention. Without it the role has no rights on public.* until it explicitly
runs `set local role authenticated` — a query before that fails with permission
denied. Fail-closed in the database rather than in application code.

The role is created idempotently. Roles are cluster-wide, not per-database, so
`supabase db reset` leaves them behind and a bare CREATE ROLE would fail on the
second reset — and two consecutive resets are the definition of done for
migrations here. The else branch also repairs a role left over with different
attributes.

No password in the migration: that would put it in git. Provisioned out of band;
ci.yml sets a local one for the smokes.

## Startup gate

main.ts and worker.ts verify the connected role before serving or working and
refuse to start on superuser, BYPASSRLS or INHERIT. A connection failure is also
a refusal — an unreachable database must not silently skip a security check,
which is the "skip that turns a mandatory gate green" CLAUDE.md forbids.

Both entrypoints take an injection point for the reader so tests need no
database, mirroring the existing DATABASE_PING token. The production path runs
through the default and is exercised by the smokes.

## CI

The "dependency down -> ready 503" smoke is replaced by two role-gate smokes:
the API must refuse to start when the role cannot be verified, and must refuse
to start as postgres. The second is the non-vacuity check — without it the gate
could be green while testing nothing. Readiness 503 keeps its coverage in
health.e2e.test.ts, which is where it belongs: readiness describes a running
process whose dependency fails, not one that was never allowed to start.

## Architecture rule

The review's sharpest point: pg is already a dependency, so a repository doing
`import { Pool } from "pg"` with config.databaseUrl would pass all nine required
checks and query with no tenant context at all — around the transaction
boundary, the role switch and RLS.

Closed with api-dependency-allowlist: outside apps/api/src/platform/, only the
listed packages may be imported. An allowlist, not a driver blocklist — the same
lesson domain-allowlist already records, since a blocklist would have to
enumerate pg-pool, postgres, typeorm, drizzle-orm and every future SDK. Proven
red against a planted pg import. pg-database-ping.ts moves into
platform/database/ because that is what it is.

BREAKING: DATABASE_URL must now name easytree_app, not postgres. An existing
deployment pointed at a superuser will refuse to start — deliberately.

Deferred, with reasons: Kysely, generated database types and the transactional
outbox. Type generation needs a live database that only db-gates has, and the
outbox has no business table to roll back with; both belong with EYT-86.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Task S3-08 of the Sprint 3 plan. **Contains a breaking change and a security fix that predates the ticket.**

## The defect the design review uncovered

ADR-001 line 85: *"Normale Runtime-Credentials dürfen RLS nicht umgehen."*

Verified against the repository:

| evidence | finding |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.example:10`, `ci.yml:213/222/230` | every `DATABASE_URL` used the **`postgres`** login role |
| `app.module.ts:33` | handed straight to the runtime |

| `0002_tenancy.sql:151-152` | says it itself: FORCE RLS bites *"sobald der Owner kein BYPASSRLS-Attribut trägt"* |

`postgres` is a superuser, and superusers bypass Row Level Security entirely. **Every policy in `0002_tenancy.sql` was ineffective for the application.** The tenant tests only prove them because they explicitly issue `set local role authenticated` — nothing in `src/` did.

No TypeScript construct fixes this. It needs a different role.

## Migration 0003: `easytree_app`

`login`, `nosuperuser`, `nobypassrls`, and **`noinherit`**.

`NOINHERIT` is the actual safeguard, not a detail. With inheritance the role holds `authenticated`'s table rights immediately, so a query issued *before* the tenant context was set would still return data — the context would be a convention. Without it, `easytree_app` has **no rights on `public.*`** until it explicitly runs `set local role authenticated`; a query before that fails with `permission denied`. Fail-closed in the database, not in application code.

**Idempotent on purpose.** Roles are cluster-wide, not per-database. `supabase db reset` leaves them behind, so a bare `CREATE ROLE` fails on the **second** reset — and two consecutive resets are the definition of done for migrations here. The `else` branch also repairs a role left over with different attributes.

**No password in the migration** — that would put it in git. Provisioned out of band; `ci.yml` sets a local one for the smokes.

`supabase/tests/0003_app_role.sql` asserts all four attributes, the membership, *and* that `easytree_app` has no `select` on `public.items` without the role switch — with a counter-check that `authenticated` does, so the test cannot pass merely because the grants are missing.

## Startup gate

`main.ts` and `worker.ts` verify the connected role before serving and refuse to start on superuser, `BYPASSRLS` or `INHERIT`.

**A connection failure is also a refusal.** An unreachable database must not silently skip a security check — that is the *"skip that turns a mandatory gate green"* `CLAUDE.md` forbids.

Both entrypoints take an injection point for the reader so tests need no database, mirroring the existing `DATABASE_PING` token. The production path runs through the default and is exercised by the smokes; two tests assert the **wiring**, not just the pure function.

## The sharpest review finding

> `pg` is already a dependency. A repository doing `import { Pool } from "pg"` with `config.databaseUrl` passes all nine required checks and queries with **no tenant context at all** — around the transaction boundary, the role switch and RLS.

Closed with `api-dependency-allowlist`: outside `apps/api/src/platform/`, only listed packages may be imported. An **allowlist**, not a driver blocklist — the same lesson `domain-allowlist` already records, since a blocklist would have to enumerate `pg-pool`, `postgres`, `typeorm`, `drizzle-orm` and every future SDK.

Proven red against a planted import:

```
apps/api/src/modules/planning/infrastructure/leak.ts:1 [api-dependency-allowlist]
"pg" steht nicht auf der Importliste von apps/api/src …
```

`pg-database-ping.ts` moves into `platform/database/` because that is what it is.

## CI change worth reviewing carefully

The `dependency down → ready 503` smoke is **replaced**. Since the bootstrap now refuses to start when the role cannot be verified, that smoke can no longer pass — the two properties are both correct but describe different moments.

Two smokes take its place: the API must refuse to start when the role cannot be verified, and must refuse to start **as `postgres`**. The second is the non-vacuity check; without it the gate could be green while testing nothing.

Readiness 503 keeps its coverage in `health.e2e.test.ts` (two cases, `DATABASE_PING` overridden via DI). That is where it belongs: readiness describes a *running* process whose dependency fails, not one that was never allowed to start.

## ⚠️ Breaking

`DATABASE_URL` must now name `easytree_app`, not `postgres`. An existing deployment pointed at a superuser **will refuse to start** — deliberately. No production deployment exists yet, so nothing is currently affected.

## Honest acceptance-criteria scorecard

| AC | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Tenantgebundene Repositories arbeiten nur innerhalb eines verifizierten Transaktionskontexts | **partial** — the *credential* half is now real and enforced at three layers (role attributes, startup gate, import allowlist). The *transaction handle* half is not built: there is no business table to write to, so a `UnitOfWork` would have no caller and its test would be its only consumer. |
| Datenbanktypen werden aus dem Schema generiert | **NOT MET** — generation needs a live database, which only `db-gates` has, and there is no business schema to generate from. Belongs with EYT-86. |
| Businesswrite und Outbox rollen gemeinsam zurück | **NOT MET** — there is no business table. A rollback proof over the synthetic `items` table would demonstrate nothing about a real domain write. |
| Parallele Requests verlieren oder vermischen keinen Tenantkontext | **NOT MET as a new proof** — the existing tenant gates cover transaction-local reset on one connection. The review showed they do *not* prove isolation across a shared Supavisor server connection (`grep pg_backend_pid` returns nothing repo-wide), and the design's proposed measurement was unsound. Recorded rather than faked. |
| Parameterisiertes SQL ist der dokumentierte Escape Hatch | **NOT MET** — no query layer in this PR. |

One of five met, one partial, three not met. **EYT-45 stays open.** What landed is the part that was both reachable and urgent; the rest genuinely needs EYT-86's schema. Splitting it that way is a proposal — say the word if you would rather see the ticket cut differently.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck` 9/9, `pnpm lint` 6/6, `pnpm test` 9/9, prettier clean, `[architecture] files=90 imports=262 rules=8 violations=0`, 69 api tests. `scripts/verify-branch-protection.sh` reports no drift — no new CI job, only changed steps inside `db-gates`.

    timeModel: { type: 'string' },
    deleteRules: { type: 'string' },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SCHEMA_RLS = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['policyPattern', 'grantTarget', 'crossTenantProof', 'failClosedRisks', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    policyPattern: { type: 'string' },
    grantTarget: { type: 'string' },
    crossTenantProof: { type: 'string' },
    failClosedRisks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SCHEMA_SCOPE = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['minimumForSlice', 'deferred', 'seedStrategy', 'acReachability', 'citations'],
  properties: {
    minimumForSlice: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    deferred: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    seedStrategy: { type: 'string' },
    acReachability: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['ac', 'reachable', 'reason'],
        properties: {
          ac: { type: 'string' },
          reachable: { type: 'string', enum: ['YES', 'PARTIAL', 'NO'] },
          reason: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    citations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const [tables, rls, scope] = await parallel([
  () => agent(CONTEXT + [
    '',
    'TASK 1 — the tables themselves. Design the core schema concretely: columns, types, keys, FKs.',
    '',
    'Answer precisely:',
    '- Which tables are tenant-owned and which are not? organizations and users are not — justify',
    '  every other decision the same way.',
    '- Composite unique (id, org_id): which tables need it, and which FKs become tenant-bound',
    '  because of it? Show one concrete FK definition.',
    '- The time model. packages/domain stores UTC instants (TimeInterval over epoch ms) and derives',
    '  the ISO week from an IANA zone (planning-week.ts). The transport uses ISO strings',
    '  (packages/contracts). What does the DATABASE store? Consider tstzrange versus two timestamptz',
    '  columns, where the IANA zone lives (per organisation? per worksite?), and whether a generated',
    '  local business date column is worth it given EYT-74 already buckets weeks in TypeScript.',
    '  Argue rather than assert.',
    '- Delete versus archive per table. PRD requires historical assignments and audit data to',
    '  survive employee deactivation. Which FKs are ON DELETE CASCADE, which RESTRICT, which rows',
    '  are never deleted?',
    '- How to split this into vertical migrations rather than one large file, with the NNNN sequence.',
  ].join('\n'), { label: 'tables', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_TABLES }),

  () => agent(CONTEXT + [
    '',
    'TASK 2 — RLS, grants and the cross-tenant proof. Migration 0002 is the pattern; read every',
    'policy in it and state the exact shape to repeat.',
    '',
    'Answer precisely:',
    '- The application now connects as easytree_app, NOINHERIT and a member of authenticated.',
    '  Which role must the GRANTs target? What happens if a new table grants to easytree_app',
    '  instead — verify against how 0002 grants.',
    '- app.current_user_id() and app.user_org_ids() are security definer with search_path empty.',
    '  Read them. Do new policies use them unchanged, or does anything need extending?',
    '- RLS scopes to the UNION of the user active orgs, so a user in two organisations sees both.',
    '  Is that right for this product, and where does single-org-per-request narrowing belong —',
    '  policy, application, or both? Cite what the tenant tests currently prove.',
    '- The pgTAP cross-tenant proof: what must it assert per table, and what would make it VACUOUS?',
    '  Read supabase/tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql and say concretely how a new table could be added',
    '  such that the existing suite stays green while that table is wide open.',
    '- FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set in 0002. Given 0003 introduced a non-superuser role, does',
    '  FORCE now actually bite? Explain precisely what changed.',
  ].join('\n'), { label: 'rls-and-grants', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_RLS }),

  () => agent(CONTEXT + [
    '',
    'TASK 3 — scope, seed and honest reachability. The ticket names eleven entity groups; the',
    'sprint-goal slice EYT-50 needs far fewer.',
    '',
    'Answer precisely:',
    '- Read docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md section S3-12 and',
    '  packages/contracts/src/planning/schemas.ts. What is the SMALLEST table set that makes the',
    '  EYT-50 reference flow work end to end? Name them.',
    '- Which of the eleven groups should be deferred, to which ticket, and why is deferring them not',
    '  laziness? The standard here is explicit: a table nobody writes is the schema equivalent of',
    '  dead code, and the last four PRs were each criticised for shipping unwired artifacts.',
    '- The seed: supabase/seed.sql holds synthetic data with fixed UUIDs. Read it. How should it',
    '  grow, and what would violate "keine personenbezogenen Produktionsdaten"?',
    '- AC5 says invariants from EYT-49 are protected transactionally — but EYT-49 is a SEPARATE open',
    '  ticket that adds the exclusion constraints. Is AC5 reachable inside EYT-86, or does it depend',
    '  on EYT-49 landing first? The sprint plan records this as a circular dependency in section',
    '  L-5 — read it and say how it should be resolved.',
    '- Judge every one of the seven acceptance criteria: YES / PARTIAL / NO with a file-grounded',
    '  reason.',
  ].join('\n'), { label: 'scope-and-seed', phase: 'Recherche', schema: SCHEMA_SCOPE }),
])

log('Recherche fertig. Tabellen vorgeschlagen: ' + (tables ? tables.tables.length : 0))

phase('Adversarial')

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['fatalFlaws', 'bypass', 'verdict', 'requiredChanges'],
  properties: {
    fatalFlaws: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    bypass: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete SQL or scenario crossing a tenant boundary while db-gates stays green; empty string if none' },
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['SOUND', 'NEEDS_CHANGES', 'REJECT'] },
    requiredChanges: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const design = JSON.stringify({ tables, rls, scope }, null, 2)

const [refuteTenant, refuteMigration] = await parallel([
  () => agent(CONTEXT + [
    '',
    'Adversarial reviewer. REFUTE this schema design, focusing on TENANT ISOLATION. Default to',
    'finding it broken. Verify every cited path and line against the real files.',
    '',
    'PROPOSED DESIGN:',
    design,
    '',
    'Attack:',
    '1. Write the concrete SQL by which organisation A reads or writes organisation B rows while',
    '   db-gates stays green. Consider: a table with RLS enabled but no policy, a policy with USING',
    '   but no WITH CHECK, an FK that is not tenant-bound, a join through a weaker table, a security',
    '   definer function, and a sequence or default that leaks.',
    '2. Which proposed table could be added such that the EXISTING pgTAP suite stays green while',
    '   that table is open? Answer with the actual file.',
    '3. The app connects as easytree_app (NOINHERIT, member of authenticated). Does every proposed',
    '   GRANT actually reach it? A grant to the wrong role produces permission denied at runtime',
    '   while all tests pass, because the tests connect differently — check how',
    '   apps/api/test/tenant-context.helper.ts connects versus how the application does.',
    '4. Does anything let the app read a table BEFORE the role switch to authenticated?',
  ].join('\n'), { label: 'refute:tenant-isolation', phase: 'Adversarial', schema: VERDICT }),

  () => agent(CONTEXT + [
    '',
    'Adversarial reviewer focused on MIGRATION SAFETY and SCOPE HONESTY.',
    '',
    'PROPOSED DESIGN:',
    design,
    '',
    'Attack:',
    '1. Reproducibility. Migration 0003 had to be idempotent because roles are cluster-wide and',
    '   survive a db reset. Does anything here share that property — extensions, roles,',
    '   publications, grants on non-database objects? Name each one that fails on the SECOND reset.',
    '2. Append-only. Does any part amount to editing a merged migration? Does it drop or alter',
    '   anything from 0001/0002/0003, and if so is there a documented forward-fix and rollback?',
    '3. Dead schema. Which proposed tables would have no writer and no reader after this PR? The',
    '   standard here is explicit: an unwired artifact is criticised, not praised. Produce the',
    '   honest list.',
    '4. AC5 depends on EYT-49, a separate open ticket. Is the design quietly claiming it? Read the',
    '   sprint plan section L-5.',
    '5. Produce the corrected per-AC scorecard yourself, file-grounded, with PARTIAL and NO rows',
    '   where deserved.',
  ].join('\n'), { label: 'refute:migration-scope', phase: 'Adversarial', schema: VERDICT }),
])

return { tables, rls, scope, adversarial: { tenant: refuteTenant, migration: refuteMigration } }

## Entscheidung

**EasyTree-master wird das einzige kanonische Produkt-Repository.** Die beiden Vite-Repositories werden nicht über Netzwerk- oder Repository-Schnittstellen miteinander gekoppelt, sondern als UX-Referenzen und Quellmodule in das Monorepo migriert.

## Beste Übergabeschnittstelle

Die passende Naht ist ein **gemeinsamer, versionierter Domain- und API-Vertrag**:

```text
Planer-UI                         Mitarbeiter-UI
(EasyTree-UIUX)                  (EasyTree-App-UI)
       \                              /
        \  typed UI ports/gateways   /
         v                          v
        packages/contracts + packages/domain
                       |
                       v
              NestJS Application API
                       |
             Domain Commands / Queries

Required by apps/api/src/modules/workforce/domain/employee.ts:10-16 (Employee{id,orgId,displayName,active}) and by the EYT-50 AC 'Mitarbeiter und Baustelle über Domain Commands' (docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md:397). public.worksites — org_id NOT NULL, unique(id, org_id), name. Required by apps/api/src/modules/worksites/domain/worksite.ts:4-14 and the same EYT-50 AC (plan:397).

public.worksite_activities — org_id NOT NULL, tenant-bound FK (worksite_id, org_id) -> worksites(id, org_id). This is the borderline one and I would argue it in review: it is the only honest producer of Worksite.activityCount (worksite.ts:13, whose comment already parks it on EYT-86) and therefore of the frozen conflict code WORKSITE_NOT_PUBLISHABLE (packages/contracts/src/planning/schemas.ts:58-63). If EYT-50 does not exercise the publishability path, drop this table and record explicitly that a frozen transport code has no producer — the repo already set that precedent by REMOVING RESOURCE_DOUBLE_BOOKED for exactly that reason (apps/api/src/modules/planning/domain/assignment-draft.ts:28-34).

public.assignments (draft) — org_id NOT NULL, unique(id, org_id), tenant-bound FKs (employee_id, org_id) and (worksite_id, org_id) following the 0002 pattern (supabase/migrations/20260723222457_0002_tenancy.sql:74-76), start_utc/end_utc timestamptz, CHECK end_utc > start_utc, a tstzrange column for EYT-49 to attach to, plus the local business date column (AC4). public.plan_versions — org_id NOT NULL, unique(id, org_id), week_key, version_no, published_at_utc, published_by, unique(org_id, week_key, version_no). Carrier of PublishedPlanVersionSchema (packages/contracts/src/planning/schemas.ts:151-158) and of PlanningWindow.publishedVersionId (schemas.ts:107-108), which the stale-version check in PublishPlanCommand (schemas.ts:136-149) compares against.

public.plan_version_assignments — immutable snapshot rows (org_id, plan_version_id, assignment_id, employee_id, tstzrange), no UPDATE/DELETE grant. EYT-50 AC 'genau einen idempotenten Workerjob' (plan:399) and EYT-45 'Businesswrite und Outbox-Eintrag rollen gemeinsam zurück' (plan:324-325). L-12 (plan:175-179) already scopes this correctly: the sprint delivers table + transaction semantics, the pg-boss delivery path stays open. The repo already enforces this standard in three places and would be inconsistent if EYT-86 broke it — SCAFFOLDED_MODULES contains only workforce/worksites/planning because 'leere Modulverzeichnisse sind keine Grenzen, sondern Scheinkapselung mit grünem Haken' (apps/api/src/modules/module-catalogue.ts:72-86); RESOURCE_DOUBLE_BOOKED was deleted from the conflict codes because 'ein deklarierter Code ohne Produzent liest sich für jeden Downstream-Leser wie "ist behandelt"' (assignment-draft.ts:28-34); and packages/contracts/src/employee/schemas.ts:4-9 carries an explicit 'Ehrlichkeitshinweis' that its schemas are a contract, not evidence of logic. Shipping eleven entity groups would produce ~30 tables of which ~8 have a writer — the same unwired-artifact criticism the last four PRs took. Each deferral below names the ticket that will WRITE the table, which is the only defensible trigger.

Skill / Certification / EmployeeSkill → NO ticket in the sprint plan (S3-01..S3-18) reads or writes a skill; needs a new backlog ticket. Nothing in packages/domain, packages/contracts or apps/api/src/modules references skills today.

Vehicle / Equipment / ResourceReservation / ConditionReport → defer to the ticket that models resource reservations. Confirmation / Rejection → defer to EYT-81 (S3-17, plan:466 'Bestätigung/Ablehnung'), the first ticket that actually wires them. The transport already exists (packages/contracts/src/employee/schemas.ts:34-61) and says in writing there is no model, table or route. GAP TO RECORD: S3-17's deliverables (plan:462-472) list no migration, so the schema owner for these tables is currently nobody.

AbsenceRequest / AbsenceDecision → defer to EYT-81 / a dedicated absence ticket. CAUTION: this directly contradicts apps/api/src/modules/module-catalogue.ts:53-55, which names EYT-86 as the ticket that introduces AbsenceRequest/AbsenceDecision. If deferred, that comment must be amended in the same PR, or the repo keeps a stale claim — the exact class of drift CLAUDE.md's evidence rules target.

HOW IT SHOULD GROW. (1) Keep the existing shape: fixed UUIDs with the encoded convention already relied on by the tests — organizations …00a1/…00b2, users …aaa1/…bbb2/…ccc3, memberships …0e0aa1, items …0110a1/…0220b2 (supabase/seed.sql:5-69). New entities continue the pattern (e.g. employees …0410a1/…0420b2, worksites …0510a1/…0520b2), because supabase/tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:41 does IDOR by hardcoding a known FOREIGN uuid — cross-tenant negatives are impossible without deterministic ids on the other side. (2) Seed BOTH tenants symmetrically. Every new tenant-owned table needs at least one Org Alpha row and one Org Beta row, or AC3's cross-tenant negative test for that table degenerates into is_empty over an empty table, which passes vacuously. (3) Keep `on conflict … do nothing` on every insert (seed.sql:9,32,40,51,60,69,79) and keep the auth.users caveat block verbatim (seed.sql:12-17) — direct insert into auth.users is local-stack-only; in real environments only GoTrue writes it. (4) Keep the reserved domain: user-a@example.test (seed.sql:24). RFC 6761 guarantees it can never belong to a real person. (5) NO passwords, not even for easytree_app — 20260727004500_0003_app_role.sql:80-87 deliberately keeps the role password out of git; the seed must not become the loophole. (6) WHAT THE SEED MUST NOT CONTAIN, and this is the sharp one: the plan data under test. EYT-50's AC says 'Mitarbeiter und Baustelle werden über Domain Commands angelegt' (plan:397). If the seed ships a ready-made employee+worksite+assignment for the reference flow, the E2E proves reading, not the write path, and the AC is quietly downgraded. The seed should provide the tenant boundary and identities (2 orgs, planner user with an active membership, an inactive membership, a counter-tenant with rows for the negatives) — and let the slice create its own employees/worksites/assignments through the API. (7) Add the org time_zone value explicitly (Europe/Berlin per ADR-002/plan:257-258) rather than relying on a column default, so a reader of the seed sees which week rule the fixtures assume.

WHAT WOULD VIOLATE 'keine personenbezogenen Produktionsdaten': any row taken from the pilot company or any production/staging dump — real employee names, addresses, phone numbers, birthdates, personnel numbers or real login e-mails; real customer worksite addresses or geo coordinates (S3-16 already bans browser geocoding for a related reason, plan:453-454); real photos or audio in storage.objects; and above all free-text fields that carry special-category data — absence reasons, sickness status (ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS_v1.3.md:99 treats 'reiner Krankheitsstatus' as its own shortest-retention category) and RejectAssignmentCommand.reason (packages/contracts/src/employee/schemas.ts:48-51), which is a min(3) free-text field and therefore the most likely place a real quote gets pasted in. CLAUDE.md:180-181 bans logging private origins, medical details, credentials, tokens and raw audio; the seed is held to the same line, and supabase/seed.sql:2 plus docs/runbooks/database-workflow.md:11 already say 'ausschließlich synthetische Daten'.

HONEST LIMIT: there is no automated PII gate. The secret-scan job only checks tracked .env/.pem/.key files and runs gitleaks (.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-94); db-gates only proves the seed LOADS (ci.yml:103-110). AC7 therefore rests on review discipline, not on a check — report it that way instead of implying a gate exists. A grep for German names would be theatre and should not be added.

Two conditions must be honoured or the second reset fails: filenames must carry the NNNN the CLI does not emit — next is <timestamp>_0004_<slug>.sql (CLAUDE.md:160-163), and any CLUSTER-wide object must be written idempotently the way 20260727004500_0003_app_role.sql:34-56 handles the role. If EYT-86 pre-creates btree_gist for EYT-49, it must be 'create extension if not exists'.

acReachability.reason: FKs and uniqueness are straightforward and have a proven pattern (unique(id, org_id) + tenant-bound composite FK, 0002_tenancy.sql:49-79). Ownership documentation has a vehicle — TABLE_OWNERSHIP (apps/api/src/modules/module-catalogue.ts:93-142) — but grep shows that constant has no reader anywhere in apps/api outside its own file, so adding eight tables without registry entries would fail nothing. Recommend a check inside the existing unit-tests job (no new CI job, per the constraint and plan:222-229) that parses 'create table public.' out of supabase/migrations/*.sql and asserts each has an entry. Two things stay open by construction: module-catalogue.ts:14-27 hands the 'one DB role per module' decision to EYT-86 — record the decision (recommendation: keep the single authenticated role and do NOT report ADR-001:78 satisfied, per CLAUDE.md:227-230); and Lösch-/Archivregeln can only be documented as INTENT — the retention table in ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS_v1.3.md:90-108 is explicitly provisional and 'rechtsgeprüfte Retention' is still listed as open at line 114, so no deletion job may be built on it.

acReachability.reason: Fully reachable inside EYT-86; the pattern is proven and re-usable line by line. Per new table: revoke all from anon (0002_tenancy.sql:132-133), grant select/insert/update/delete to authenticated — NOT to easytree_app, which is NOINHERIT and must stay privilege-free until 'set local role authenticated' (0003_app_role.sql:59-72, asserted by supabase/tests/0003_app_role.sql:61-71) — then enable + force RLS and add org_id in (select app.user_org_ids()) policies (0002_tenancy.sql:154-222). acReachability.ac: Zeitwerte verwenden UTC-Instants plus IANA-Zeitzone und lokale Geschaeftsdaten.
acReachability.reason: The semantics are already defined and tested in the domain — localBusinessDate via Intl.formatToParts (packages/domain/src/planning-week.ts:98-115), ISO-8601 week rule (planning-week.ts:24-31), and the requirement text itself is INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md:106. The missing carrier is organizations.time_zone, which planning-week.ts:75-76 explicitly parks on EYT-86. ONE UNVERIFIED DESIGN RISK, flagged rather than asserted: a GENERATED STORED local-date column derived from a timestamptz is likely rejected, because timezone(text, timestamptz) is STABLE not IMMUTABLE and generated columns/CHECK constraints require immutability. I did not run Postgres in this session — treat it as the first thing to test in the migration, and plan for the local date to be written by the command inside the same transaction (or a BEFORE trigger) with a comment explaining why it is not generated.

GRANTs must target `authenticated` — never `easytree_app`, and never `anon`/`public`.

Why that is the only workable target: the runtime path is connect as easytree_app → `set local role authenticated` → query (0003:59-72; the pattern lives in apps/api/test/tenant-context.helper.ts:53-57). After SET ROLE the current role is `authenticated`; privileges held directly by the session role easytree_app are no longer in effect. So a table granted only to easytree_app raises `permission denied for table …` (42501) on every real query. That is exactly what tests/0003_app_role.sql:61-71 asserts from the other direction (`has_table_privilege('easytree_app','public.items','select') = false`) with the counter-check at :77-81 that `authenticated` does hold it — i.e. the rights exist, they are simply not inherited (NOINHERIT, 0003:62-72, asserted at tests/0003:30-34).

The dangerous half: NOINHERIT blocks only membership-derived privileges — a DIRECT grant to easytree_app IS usable by easytree_app itself, before any role switch. So a table granted to easytree_app creates a second access path that runs outside the tenant context: with RLS enabled and all policies written `to authenticated`, no policy matches role easytree_app, so SELECT silently returns 0 rows and writes fail 42501 (default deny — annoying but closed). If that same migration also forgets `enable row level security`, the pre-switch query returns EVERY organisation's rows with no error at all. That combination — grant to easytree_app + missing ENABLE — is the fail-open shape this codebase is one migration away from.

Practical warning for EYT-86: when new repositories first hit `permission denied`, the reflex fix is `grant … to easytree_app`. The correct fix is always (a) grant to `authenticated`, and (b) make the data-access layer actually issue `set local role authenticated` per transaction — which no runtime code does today: grepping apps/api/src for `set local role`/`set role` finds only comments (role-privileges.ts:36, :69). ## Sequence, filenames, and why the cut is where it is

Constraint check first (all verified): filenames are `<timestamp>_NNNN_<slug>.sql` and the CLI emits only the timestamp, so every new file is renamed by hand (`CLAUDE.md:160-163`). Existing sequence is `20260723214800_0001_foundation.sql`, `20260723222457_0002_tenancy.sql`, `20260727004500_0003_app_role.sql` (directory listing). Next free number is **0004**; every new timestamp must sort after `20260727004500`. Definition of done is two consecutive `db reset` plus green `supabase test db` (`docs/runbooks/database-workflow.md:39`), which `db-gates` already runs twice each (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:103-110`) — **no new CI job is needed or wanted**.

Postgres is `major_version = 17` (`supabase/config.toml:42`). That rules out PG18 temporal keys (`PRIMARY KEY … WITHOUT OVERLAPS`); overlap protection must be `EXCLUDE USING gist`, which is what the sprint plan already prescribes (`docs/plans/2026-07-26-eyt-sprint-3-integrierter-slice.md:366`).

### Ten vertical migrations, one bounded context each

| # | Filename | Content | Why its own file |
| - | -------- | ------- | ---------------- |
| 0004 | `<ts>_0004_org_settings.sql` | `organizations.time_zone`; enable+force RLS **on `organizations` itself**; select-policy + grant; time-zone validation trigger; widen `memberships.role` check | Every later migration depends on the org time zone existing. Also closes a live hole (below). |
| 0005 | `<ts>_0005_workforce.sql` | `employees`, `skills`, `employee_skills` | Referenced by planning, absence and timekeeping — must land before them. |
| 0006 | `<ts>_0006_worksites.sql` | `worksites` (incl. meeting-point columns), `activities` | Independent of 0005; ordered before planning. |
| 0007 | `<ts>_0007_resources.sql` | `resources`, `resource_reservations`, `condition_reports` | Reservations reference assignments **nullably**, so this can precede planning; if you prefer a hard FK, move reservations into 0008. |
| 0008 | `<ts>_0008_planning.sql` | `plan_versions`, `assignments` | The core. Needs 0005 + 0006. |
| 0009 | `<ts>_0009_confirmation.sql` | `plan_confirmations`, `assignment_rejections` | Needs 0008. Small, high-review-value file. |
| 0010 | `<ts>_0010_absence.sql` | `absence_requests`, `absence_decisions` | Needs 0005 only. |
| 0011 | `<ts>_0011_timekeeping.sql` | `time_entries`, `time_corrections`, one-active-timer partial unique index | Needs 0005 + 0008. |
| 0012 | `<ts>_0012_audit_outbox.sql` | `audit_events`, `outbox_messages`, `idempotency_keys`, `app.write_audit()` / `app.enqueue_outbox()` | Deliberately last: the only file installing SECURITY DEFINER writers, so it gets its own review. |
| 0013 | `<ts>_0013_btree_gist.sql` | `create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;` | Isolated so EYT-49 can add `EXCLUDE` constraints in 0014+ without touching any EYT-86 file. `0001_foundation.sql:9` shows `pgtap` is currently the **only** extension. |

Matching pgTAP files `supabase/tests/0004_*.sql` … `0013_*.sql` (the suite is discovered by glob; `0001_smoke.sql` / `0002_rls_isolation.sql` / `0003_app_role.sql` are the pattern).

### Scope: I follow the ticket's entity list, not the plan's superset

The plan's S3-09 entity list (`sprint-3:334-340`) is wider than the ticket's. Weather (`WeatherSnapshot`/`WeatherWarning`), `Notification`, `Conflict`, `ValidationResult`, `AssignmentChange` and `Permission` are **not** in EYT-86's entity list and get no table here. `permissions` in particular would require inventing a product-defined permission catalogue that exists nowhere in the repo (grep finds no list), and `module-catalogue.ts:72-81` explicitly warns that empty structure with a green check is worse than an honest gap. Outbox *is* included despite not being named, because L-12 (`sprint-3:175-179`) records that the transactional outbox has no owning ticket while EYT-45 requires "Businesswrite und zugehöriger Outbox-Eintrag rollen gemeinsam zurück" — that test cannot exist without the table.

### No new module slug for absence

`MODULE_SLUGS` is frozen (`module-catalogue.ts:57-68`) and `module-catalogue.ts:50-55` says explicitly that `absence` is "NICHT vorsorglich angelegt, sondern von dem Ticket entschieden, das Abwesenheiten modelliert (EYT-86)". **Decision: absences are owned by `workforce`**, not by a new module — adding a slug would force a new directory with `domain/` + `application/` + `index.ts` files (`module-catalogue.ts:78-81`) that this ticket does not write. `TABLE_OWNERSHIP` (`module-catalogue.ts:111-142`) must be extended in the same PR; it is documentation, not enforcement (`module-catalogue.ts:14-27`), and reporting it as enforcement is forbidden.

### A live hole 0004 must close

`public.organizations` is created in `0001_foundation.sql:20-24` and then **never** gets `enable row level security`, never gets `force`, never gets a policy, and is absent both from the `revoke … from anon` list (`0002_tenancy.sql:132-133`) and from the RLS assertions in `supabase/tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:238-257`, which cover only `users`, `memberships`, `items`, `item_notes`. The tenant root is the one table with no RLS. 0004 must `enable` + `force` RLS on it, `grant select` (only) to `authenticated`, add `create policy organizations_select_own … using (id in (select app.user_org_ids()))`, and extend the pgTAP RLS assertions. Without it the app cannot legitimately read its own org's `time_zone` anyway.

### Fix-forward items in 0004 (never edit a merged file)

- `memberships.role` currently checks `in ('owner','member')` (`0002_tenancy.sql:36`), but PRD §2 defines three business roles and says each user has exactly one (`CURRENT_PRD_v1.3.md:19-39`). 0004 does `alter table public.memberships drop constraint <name>, add constraint memberships_role_check check (role in (…))`. Dropping a constraint in a *new* migration is fix-forward and allowed (`database-workflow.md:10`); editing `0002` is not. The existing constraint name is Postgres-generated and I could not read it (`\d` needs a running DB; Docker is down) — **unverified**; read it from the live catalogue rather than assuming `memberships_role_check`.
- `public.items` / `public.item_notes` are **not** dropped. `supabase/tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:27-31,220-229`, `supabase/seed.sql:53-69` and `apps/api/test/tenant-context.helper.ts:20-21` all depend on them; removing them would turn a required gate red. They stay in `TABLE_OWNERSHIP` with `owner: null` (`module-catalogue.ts:130-141`); retiring them is a separate ticket.

### Boilerplate every table file repeats (fail-closed, from 0002)

1. `revoke all on table … from anon;` (`0002_tenancy.sql:132-133`)
2. `grant select, insert, update, delete on table … to authenticated;` — **to `authenticated`, never to `easytree_app`**. `easytree_app` is `NOINHERIT` and reaches privileges only through `set local role authenticated` (`0003_app_role.sql:46-53,62-72`); granting to the login role directly defeats that, and `supabase/tests/0003_app_role.sql:61-71` asserts against it.
3. `alter table … enable row level security; alter table … force row level security;` (`0002_tenancy.sql:154-161`)
4. Four policies `to authenticated` using `org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())` (`0002_tenancy.sql:189-204`). No `service_role` policy — `0002_rls_isolation.sql:259-265` asserts none exists.
5. Append-only tables get `grant select` only plus a SECURITY DEFINER writer in schema `app` (the `app.user_org_ids()` pattern, `0002_tenancy.sql:102-121`). No insert grant means audit rows cannot be forged by ordinary module code; no update/delete grant makes append-only a *privilege*, not a convention.

### Rollback / forward-fix, per migration (AC 6)

Each file carries a `-- Rollback:` header block. Because merged migrations are append-only (`CLAUDE.md:156-158`, `database-workflow.md:10`), "rollback" has exactly two legal meanings and both are written down per file:

- **Pre-merge / local:** discard the file and `supabase db reset`. The database is disposable by design (`database-workflow.md:41-49`).
- **Post-merge:** a *new* numbered migration that reverses the change, with the exact statements pre-written in the header (e.g. `drop table if exists public.assignments;` in reverse dependency order). For 0004's `alter` statements the reverse is spelled out explicitly (`alter table public.organizations drop column time_zone;`).

Because these reversals are destructive, `CLAUDE.md:176-177` applies: no destructive migration without an approved rollback **and restore evidence**. That is satisfiable today only because production is not released (`CURRENT_PRD_v1.3.md:5`, `:196`). The header therefore states plainly that in production the rollback path is restore-from-backup, not a down-migration.

### Seed (AC 7)

Extend `supabase/seed.sql` in the existing style — synthetic only, fixed UUIDs (`supabase/seed.sql:1-3`, required by `database-workflow.md:11`). Employees `Mitarbeiter Alpha 1/2`, worksite `Baustelle Alpha Nord`, skill `Seilklettertechnik`. No real names, addresses or medical detail (`CLAUDE.md:181`). State honestly: "no personal data" cannot be proven by a test, only by review — do not report it as machine-verified.

tables.rationale: FK target of assignments and confirmations → composite unique required. week_key is STORED as a key, not re-derived: the ISO-week rule lives once, in packages/domain/src/planning-week.ts:133-143, and the regex here is byte-identical to the transport contract at packages/contracts/src/planning/schemas.ts:96. Writing extract(isoyear/week ...) in SQL would be a second implementation of exactly the rule FIND-003 broke. version_no supports the stale-version check that PublishPlanCommandSchema.expectedVersionId already assumes (schemas.ts:144-149). ADR-001:89 requires plan revisions to stay historically referenceable.

tables.name: public.assignments
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (id, org_id); fk (plan_version_id, org_id) cascade; fk (employee_id, org_id) restrict; fk (worksite_id, org_id) restrict; fk (activity_id, org_id) restrict, nullable; starts_at_utc / ends_at_utc timestamptz; local_date date; during tstzrange generated stored; check (ends_at_utc > starts_at_utc)
tables.rationale: The centre of the schema and the table with the most tenant-bound FKs. unique (id, org_id) is required because rejections, time_entries and reservations all point at an assignment tenant-bound. The half-open CHECK mirrors the domain invariant one-for-one (time-interval.ts:126-130, doc :53-58). The range column exists so EYT-49 can add EXCLUDE USING gist (org_id WITH =, employee_id WITH =, during WITH &&) WHERE published — assignment-draft.ts:70-74 and draft-validation.ts:19-21 both state in writing that the TypeScript check gives no concurrency guarantee and that the guarantee belongs in the database.

tables.name: public.plan_confirmations
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (org_id, plan_version_id, employee_id); fk (plan_version_id, org_id) restrict; fk (employee_id, org_id) restrict; confirmed_at_utc timestamptz not null
tables.rationale: Leaf, no composite unique. The unique triple is the whole point: one confirmation per employee per published version, so a retried request cannot double-confirm. Matches ConfirmationSchema (packages/contracts/src/employee/schemas.ts:40-45), which carries exactly versionId + confirmedAtUtc. RESTRICT on both parents; ADR-001:89 requires confirmations to remain historically referenceable.

tables.name: public.assignment_rejections
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); fk (assignment_id, org_id) on delete restrict; fk (employee_id, org_id) on delete restrict; category text check; reason text not null check (char_length(reason) between 3 and 500); rejected_at_utc timestamptz
tables.rationale: Leaf. The length CHECK is copied from the already-agreed transport shape z.string().min(3).max(500) (packages/contracts/src/employee/schemas.ts:48-51) so DB and contract cannot disagree. category is a column because PRD:53 requires 'Ablehnung mit Kategorie UND Pflichttext' — both, not either. RESTRICT to assignments: a rejected assignment must not be deletable out from under its rejection.

tables.name: public.absence_requests
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (id, org_id); fk (employee_id, org_id) on delete restrict; kind text check (kind in ('vacation','sick','other')); first_local_date date; last_local_date date; check (last_local_date >= first_local_date); status text check
tables.rationale: Owned by workforce, NOT a new 'absence' module — MODULE_SLUGS is frozen (module-catalogue.ts:57-68), :50-55 leaves the choice to this ticket, and :72-81 warns that an empty module directory is fake encapsulation with a green check. Needs unique (id, org_id) because decisions reference it. Modelled on LOCAL DATES, not instants: absence is a calendar concept and PRD:56 lists 'Urlaub, Krankheit und weitere Abwesenheiten' by day. Deliberately NO free-text note column — CLAUDE.md:181 forbids storing medical detail, and ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS_v1.3.md:99 wants pure sickness status kept 'möglichst kurz, maximal 12 Monate', which only works if there is nothing beyond the kind flag to keep.

tables.name: public.absence_decisions
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); fk (absence_request_id, org_id) on delete restrict; fk (decided_by_employee_id, org_id) on delete restrict; decision text check (decision in ('approved','rejected')); decided_at_utc timestamptz
tables.rationale: Leaf, append-only (select+insert grant only, no update/delete grant). A separate table rather than columns on the request because PRD:51 makes an approved absence a publication blocker — the decision history has to survive a later status change on the request, and an overwritten column would erase who approved what.

tables.name: public.time_entries
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (id, org_id); fk (assignment_id, org_id) restrict; fk (employee_id, org_id) restrict; started_at_utc timestamptz not null; ended_at_utc timestamptz null; local_date date; status text check; PLUS partial unique index (org_id, employee_id) where ended_at_utc is null
tables.rationale: Needs unique (id, org_id) because time_corrections reference it. ended_at_utc nullable IS the running timer — one column, not a separate ActiveTimeEntry table, which keeps 'exactly one active timer' (PRD:60) expressible as a single partial unique index. That index is plain btree, needs no btree_gist, and therefore belongs in EYT-86 rather than EYT-49. started_at_utc is a SERVER instant: FIND-006 Extreme (AUDIT_REPORT.md:35) is exactly the opposite — browser ticks and localised display time — and ActiveTimeEntrySchema (contracts/employee/schemas.ts:77-83) already commits to the instant.

tables.name: public.time_corrections
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); fk (time_entry_id, org_id) on delete restrict; fk (corrected_by_employee_id, org_id) on delete restrict; original_started_at_utc; original_ended_at_utc; corrected_started_at_utc; corrected_ended_at_utc; reason text not null; corrected_at_utc
tables.rationale: Leaf, append-only, never updated or deleted. Carries the ORIGINAL values as its own columns rather than pointing at a mutated row: PRD:61 requires 'begründete administrative Korrektur unter Erhalt des Originals' and sprint-3:365 states the invariant as 'Arbeitszeitkorrektur bewahrt Originalwert, Korrektur, Grund und Akteur' — four things, all four are columns here.

tables.name: public.audit_events
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade; actor_user_id uuid null (NO fk); subject_type text; subject_id uuid (NO fk); action text; payload jsonb; occurred_at_utc timestamptz; index (org_id, occurred_at_utc desc)
tables.rationale: Tenant-owned because ADR-001:87 requires audit records to be tenant-bound. Deliberately has NO foreign key to the subject row: a RESTRICT FK would make audit block ordinary deletions, and a CASCADE FK would destroy the audit trail exactly when it matters. subject_id plus a payload snapshot is the denormalisation that lets audit outlive its subject — the concrete mechanism behind 'audit data survives employee deactivation'. Grants: select only to authenticated; rows are written by a SECURITY DEFINER app.write_audit() following the app.user_org_ids() pattern (0002_tenancy.sql:102-121), so append-only is enforced by privilege, not convention.

tables.name: public.outbox_messages
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); org_id not null references organizations on delete cascade; topic text; payload jsonb; created_at_utc; published_at_utc null; attempts int; index (published_at_utc) where published_at_utc is null
tables.rationale: Not named in EYT-86's entity list; included because L-12 (sprint-3:175-179) records that the transactional outbox has NO owning sprint ticket while EYT-45 requires 'Businesswrite und zugehöriger Outbox-Eintrag rollen gemeinsam zurück' — that test cannot exist without the table. Tenant-bound per ADR-001:87 ('Alle Caches, Jobs, Dateien, Audit- und Idempotency-Datensätze sind tenant-gebunden'). Written through a SECURITY DEFINER enqueue function, which still runs inside the caller's transaction, so rollback semantics hold. The delivery path (pg-boss worker) stays out of scope, as L-12 states.

tables.name: public.idempotency_keys
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (org_id, key); request_fingerprint text; response_status int; response_body jsonb; created_at_utc
tables.rationale: Tenant-owned, and the unique key is (org_id, key), not (key) — packages/contracts/src/primitives.ts:86-97 states it verbatim: 'Der Schlüsselraum ist mandantengebunden ... derselbe Schlüssel in zwei Organisationen sind zwei verschiedene Vorgänge', citing ADR-001:87. Stores the first response so a retry returns it instead of a conflict (primitives.ts:93-96).

tables.name: public.items
tables.owner: none (synthetic RLS proof table, owner stays null in TABLE_OWNERSHIP)
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); unique (id, org_id) — unchanged
tables.rationale: Kept, NOT dropped. Synthetic RLS proof table (module-catalogue.ts:130-135) that merged mandatory tests depend on: tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:27-31,220-229, seed.sql:53-60, and apps/api/test/tenant-context.helper.ts:20-21. Dropping it in EYT-86 would turn a required gate red for no product reason. Retiring it is a separate ticket.

tables.name: public.item_notes
tables.owner: none (synthetic RLS proof table, owner stays null in TABLE_OWNERSHIP)
tables.keyColumns: pk (id); NO composite unique; fk (item_id, org_id) -> items(id, org_id) — unchanged
tables.rationale: Kept for the same reason as items, and it is also the reference implementation for the leaf rule: it is nobody's FK target, so it has no unique (id, org_id) (0002_tenancy.sql:67-76). Every leaf table above follows this precedent rather than adding an index that buys nothing.

## What the database stores

### The three layers that already exist, and the one gap

- **Domain** stores UTC instants as epoch milliseconds in private fields, half-open `[start, end)` (`packages/domain/src/time-interval.ts:104-134`); the half-open choice is argued at `:53-58` — `08:00-12:00` and `12:00-16:00` must not collide or every same-day site change would block publication.
- **Week derivation** converts an instant to a local calendar day and then to an ISO week, with the IANA zone as an explicit parameter and no default (`planning-week.ts:98-115`, `:133-143`, rule 3 at `:32-35`).
- **Transport** uses exactly one ISO string form: UTC, three decimals, `Z` (`packages/contracts/src/primitives.ts:28-44`), because three spellings of one instant would produce three idempotency fingerprints (`primitives.ts:16-23`).
- **Database**: nothing. `INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md:106` demands "UTC-Instants **plus** IANA-Zeitzone und lokale Geschäftsdaten" and `:107` demands half-open intervals; no migration implements either.

### Decision 1 — two `timestamptz` columns as the authored truth, plus a GENERATED STORED `tstzrange`

Not one or the other. Both, with a hard direction of derivation:

```sql
starts_at_utc timestamptz not null,
ends_at_utc   timestamptz not null,
during        tstzrange generated always as
                (tstzrange(starts_at_utc, ends_at_utc, '[)')) stored,
constraint assignments_half_open check (ends_at_utc > starts_at_utc)
```

Why the two scalar columns are the writable ones:

1. **The seam on both sides is two instants, not a range.** `TimeIntervalDtoSchema` is `{ startUtc, endUtc }` (`contracts/planning/schemas.ts:38-46`) and `TimeInterval.create(start, end)` takes two arguments (`time-interval.ts:144`). A range-only column forces a parse on every read and a construct on every write at a seam where no other layer works in ranges.
2. **`pg` cannot parse `tstzrange`.** Verified, not assumed: `node_modules/.pnpm/pg-types@2.2.0/node_modules/pg-types/lib/textParsers.js:180-211` registers `3907` (`numrange[]`) as a *string* array and registers no range OID at all — no `3908`, no `3910`, no `tstzrange`. The driver would hand the API the literal `["2026-08-03 06:00:00+00","2026-08-03 14:30:00+00")` and someone would write a hand-rolled bounds parser. A hand-rolled boundary parser is precisely the second-model bug `time-interval.ts:1-11` exists to prevent. The repo uses `pg` directly (`apps/api/test/tenant-context.helper.ts:14`).
3. **The CHECK reads like the invariant it enforces.** `ends_at_utc > starts_at_utc` is character-for-character the domain rule at `time-interval.ts:126-130`. The range equivalent (`not isempty(during) and lower_inc(during) and not upper_inc(during) and lower(during) is not null`) is four conditions a reviewer has to decode.

Why the range column exists anyway:

4. **`EXCLUDE USING gist` needs a range operand.** EYT-49's prescribed technique is `tstzrange` + partial `EXCLUDE` with `org_id` equality (`sprint-3:366-368`). Indexing a plain column is cheaper to read and to reason about than indexing an expression, and a partial index composes more cleanly on top.
5. **`GENERATED … STORED` makes drift impossible.** Same argument the codebase already makes for `Worksite.activityCount` staying derived: two writable representations of one fact will disagree eventually.
6. **Half-open is not free with ranges.** `tstzrange` is a *continuous* range, so Postgres does not normalise `[]` to `[)` the way it does for `daterange`. If the range were writable, `[a, b]` would be insertable and `&&` would report a conflict at the shared boundary — resurrecting the "Baustellenwechsel um 12:00" false conflict. Pinning `'[)'` inside a generated expression removes the possibility rather than checking for it.

**Caveat, stated as unverified:** generated-column expressions must be IMMUTABLE, and I could not confirm the volatility of the three-argument `tstzrange(timestamptz, timestamptz, text)` constructor — Docker is down here, so no catalogue query was possible. Range constructors over already-resolved `timestamptz` inputs are immutable in standard PostgreSQL, and the plan's `EXCLUDE` design (`sprint-3:366`) depends on the same property since index expressions carry the same requirement. Verify with `select provolatile from pg_proc where proname = 'tstzrange'` on the first `db reset`; if it is not `i`, both the generated column and the plan's `EXCLUDE` need rethinking — so failing there is loud, not silent.

### Decision 2 — the IANA zone lives on the ORGANISATION, not the worksite

`organizations.time_zone text not null`, one row per tenant.

Evidence, not preference:

- `packages/domain/src/planning-week.ts:75-76` says it outright: "Pilotzeitzone. Wird pro Organisation konfigurierbar, sobald EYT-86 sie trägt."
- The already-agreed transport carries **one** `timeZone` for a whole week window (`contracts/planning/schemas.ts:101-105`) and **one** for a whole employee schedule (`contracts/employee/schemas.ts:16-24`). A per-worksite zone is not expressible in either contract — a week whose sites sat in different zones would have no single week boundary to report, and the comment at `schemas.ts:103-105` ("damit die UI die Wochengrenze nicht selbst raten muss") would become false.
- A per-worksite zone would fork the week rule: `planningWeekOf` (`planning-week.ts:151-153`) takes exactly one zone, and `aggregateWeeklyLoad` buckets an employee's whole week with one zone (`weekly-capacity.ts:73-97`). Two zones in one week could put an employee's Monday and Tuesday shifts in different ISO weeks — the FIND-003 class of bug, one layer down.

Explicit non-decision, recorded rather than pre-built: a nullable `worksites.time_zone` override is **not** added. It becomes justified only when a contract change carries a per-site zone; adding it now would create a second source of truth nothing can read.

Adding the column to an existing table under append-only rules:

```sql
alter table public.organizations add column time_zone text not null default 'Europe/Berlin';
alter table public.organizations alter column time_zone drop default;
```

The default backfills the two seed rows (`supabase/seed.sql:5-9`) in the same statement; dropping it immediately afterwards forces every future insert to state the zone explicitly, matching `planning-week.ts:32-35` ("Es gibt bewusst keinen Standardwert: eine implizite Server- oder Browserzeitzone wäre exakt die Klasse Fehler, die dieses Modul behebt"). `Europe/Berlin` as the transitional backfill is defensible because it is already the repo's declared pilot constant (`planning-week.ts:76`), not an invention.

Validation cannot be a CHECK constraint: verifying an id against `pg_timezone_names` requires a subquery, which CHECK constraints forbid. Use a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF time_zone` trigger that evaluates `now() at time zone new.time_zone` and lets the `invalid_parameter_value` error surface. The TypeScript validator `createTimeZone` (`planning-week.ts:66-73`) uses `Intl` and cannot be called from SQL, so the database needs its own — and the database is the fail-closed layer.

### Decision 3 — store `local_date`; do NOT store the ISO week; do NOT make either generated

**`local_date date not null` on `assignments`, `time_entries`, `resource_reservations`. Plain column, not generated.**

Why it cannot be a generated column — two independent hard blockers:

1. A generation expression may reference **only columns of the same row**. The zone lives on `public.organizations`, a different table. Denormalising `time_zone` onto every row to work around this recreates exactly the drift the design avoids.
2. `timestamptz AT TIME ZONE <text>` resolves to `timezone(text, timestamptz)`, which is STABLE rather than IMMUTABLE because tzdata is mutable — generated columns require IMMUTABLE. *(Standard PostgreSQL behaviour; **unverified in this environment**, Docker daemon is down. Confirm with `select provolatile from pg_proc where proname = 'timezone'`. Blocker 1 alone is sufficient regardless.)*

So: the application writes `local_date`, derived by `localBusinessDate` (`planning-week.ts:98-115`) — the one function that already owns this conversion — and a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger recomputes it from `starts_at_utc` plus the org's zone and raises on mismatch. A trigger *may* call STABLE functions, which is exactly the freedom a generated column lacks. One derivation authority (TypeScript) plus a fail-closed database check, instead of two authorities that can disagree.

Subtlety for the migration comment: the trigger must fire only on INSERT and on UPDATE of the time columns, never as a bulk revalidation. After a tzdata update a historical row could legitimately recompute differently, and re-validating it would fail a write that has nothing to do with that row's correctness.

**Is `local_date` worth it at all, given EYT-74 already buckets weeks in TypeScript?** Yes, and the distinction is precise:

- The **week** is a planning/display concept. `planningWeekKey` produces `2026-W32` (`planning-week.ts:160-162`), the transport already carries it (`contracts/planning/schemas.ts:96`), and `projectWeeks` filters the existing aggregate rather than recomputing (`weekly-capacity.ts:154-160`). Writing `extract(isoyear from …)` / `extract(week from …)` in SQL would be a *second* implementation of the ISO-8601 rule defined at `planning-week.ts:133-143` — the literal FIND-003 duplication. So **no `iso_year` / `iso_week` columns**; week-window queries use `local_date >= $monday and local_date < $monday + 7`, with the Monday computed in TypeScript from the `weekKey`.
- The **day** is a storage concept SQL genuinely needs and TypeScript cannot serve: retention is specified per category at day/year granularity (`ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS_v1.3.md:94-106` — 2 years, 3 years, 90 days, 48 hours), "today's assignments" is a predicate a deletion job and an index must both use, and `absence_requests` is inherently a date range (`PRD:56`). Converting a `timestamptz` to a local day inside a `WHERE` clause defeats any index on it.

`plan_versions` stores `week_key text` with the regex CHECK copied from `contracts/planning/schemas.ts:96`. That is storing an already-computed key, not re-deriving a rule — a plan version *is* per week and needs a unique target for `unique (org_id, week_key, version_no)`.

### Summary of the stored shape

| Concept | Column(s) | Authority |
| ------- | --------- | --------- |
| Instant | `*_at_utc timestamptz` | client → contract → domain |
| Interval | `during tstzrange` GENERATED STORED `'[)'` | derived from the two instants |
| Zone | `organizations.time_zone` | org config, trigger-validated |
| Local day | `local_date date`, trigger-checked | `localBusinessDate` (TypeScript) |
| ISO week | `plan_versions.week_key text` only | `planningWeekKey` (TypeScript) |

## Delete versus archive, per table

The governing requirement: historical assignments and audit data must survive employee deactivation. `ADR-001:89` states it as "Planrevisionen, Bestätigungen und Korrekturen bleiben historisch referenzierbar", and `PRD:44` distinguishes two operations — "Mitarbeiter anlegen, bearbeiten, **deaktivieren und archivieren**". The domain already encodes half of it: `employee.ts:14-15` — "Inaktive Personen bleiben referenzierbar, sind aber nicht planbar."

### Three states, not two

- `active = false` — **deactivation.** Still visible, still referenced, not selectable for new assignments (`isAssignable`, `employee.ts:19-21`). No row is touched anywhere else.
- `archived_at is not null` — **archival.** Hidden from pickers and lists; rows survive untouched.
- `DELETE` — reserved for (a) tenant offboarding and (b) retention jobs. Never a user-facing action on a person, a site, a resource, a plan version, a time entry or an audit event.

### ON DELETE CASCADE

Every `org_id` FK to `public.organizations`, without exception. This is the existing pattern (`0002_tenancy.sql:34`, `:51`, `:69`). Deleting an organisation is tenant offboarding, and a partially-deleted tenant is worse than either outcome. `audit_events` cascades too — the tenant whose actions were logged no longer exists.

Also CASCADE:

- `activities → worksites` — an activity has no meaning without its site, and a site with published assignments is archived rather than deleted, so this never fires in practice.
- `assignments → plan_versions` — deleting a **draft** version removes its draft assignments. Published versions are undeletable (below), so no published assignment is reachable by this path.
- `resource_reservations → assignments` — a reservation exists only to serve an assignment.
- `public.users → auth.users` — pre-existing (`0002_tenancy.sql:21`). This is precisely why `employees.user_id` must **not** be a cascading FK.

### ON DELETE RESTRICT

Everything pointing at a person, a resource, a site or a time entry:

- `assignments → employees`, `assignments → worksites`, `assignments → activities`
- `time_entries → employees`, `time_entries → assignments`
- `time_corrections → time_entries`, `time_corrections → employees` (the actor)
- `absence_requests → employees`; `absence_decisions → absence_requests`, `→ employees` (the decider)
- `plan_confirmations → plan_versions`, `→ employees`
- `assignment_rejections → assignments`, `→ employees`
- `resource_reservations → resources`; `condition_reports → resources`, `→ employees`

RESTRICT does real work: it converts "someone tried to delete an employee who has history" from silent data loss into error `23503`, at the same layer where `tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:220-229` already proves cross-tenant references fail with `23503`. The application never needs to remember the rule.

**Note on nullable composite FKs:** `foreign key (activity_id, org_id) references public.activities (id, org_id)` with `activity_id` nullable uses the default `MATCH SIMPLE`, so the constraint is simply not checked when `activity_id` is NULL — which is the desired "optional reference". `MATCH FULL` would behave differently (it would reject a partially-NULL key, and `org_id` is NOT NULL). Write it down; this is the kind of detail that gets silently wrong.

### ON DELETE SET NULL — exactly one

`employees.user_id → public.users(id) on delete set null`. This is the seam where the two lifecycles meet and must not be coupled. `public.users` cascades from `auth.users` (`0002_tenancy.sql:21`), so with CASCADE here, deleting the login identity would take the employment record and — via RESTRICT everywhere else — either fail the delete or destroy history. SET NULL means revoking access severs the login while the employment record, its assignments, its time entries and its audit trail stay exactly where they are.

### No FK at all — deliberate

`audit_events.subject_id` and `audit_events.actor_user_id` carry **no** foreign key. Both alternatives are wrong: RESTRICT would make the audit log block ordinary deletions, and CASCADE would erase the audit trail at exactly the moment it becomes evidence. Instead the row carries `subject_type` + `subject_id` + a `payload jsonb` snapshot, so it stays readable after its subject is gone. This is the concrete mechanism behind "audit survives employee deactivation" — and it survives employee *deletion* too, which RESTRICT alone does not give you.

### Rows that are never deleted (privilege-enforced, not convention)

`audit_events`, `time_corrections`, `absence_decisions`, `plan_confirmations`, `assignment_rejections` and published `plan_versions` receive:

```sql
grant select on table public.audit_events to authenticated;   -- no insert/update/delete
```

Writes go through a `SECURITY DEFINER` function in schema `app`, following the existing `app.user_org_ids()` pattern (`0002_tenancy.sql:102-121`: `security definer`, `set search_path = ''`, `revoke all … from public`, `grant execute … to authenticated`). This mirrors the memberships design one step further: `memberships` already has select-only grant plus select-only policy, and `0002_tenancy.sql:181-183` explains why — "Selbst-Eskalation … ist damit doppelt (Grant + Policy) dicht", proven by `tests/0002_rls_isolation.sql:113-121`. Append-only becomes a privilege property rather than a code-review promise, and it removes the need for immutability triggers on these tables.

### Published plan versions

`plan_versions` gets a `BEFORE DELETE` and a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger that raises when `status = 'published'`. `ADR-001:89` and `sprint-3:364` ("veröffentlichte Planrevisionen nicht still überschreibbar") both require it; `PublishPlanCommandSchema.expectedVersionId` (`contracts/planning/schemas.ts:144-149`) already assumes versions are stable enough to compare against. Draft versions are freely deletable and cascade their assignments.

**Scope note, honestly stated:** the plan's L-5 resolution (`sprint-3:119-121`) assigns "Tabellen inkl. Range-Spalten" to EYT-86 and "Constraints/Trigger/pgTAP" to EYT-49. EYT-86's own AC 5 nevertheless says "Kritische Invarianten aus EYT-49 werden transaktional geschuetzt." These are in tension. My split: EYT-86 delivers what needs no `btree_gist` — the tenant-bound composite FKs (`23503` at FK level, independent of RLS, per `CLAUDE.md:145-152`), the `CHECK` invariants, the immutability triggers above, and the one-active-timer partial unique index `(org_id, employee_id) where ended_at_utc is null` (plain btree). EYT-49 delivers the `EXCLUDE USING gist` overlap constraints plus the two-session concurrency tests (`sprint-3:366-374`). Do not report EYT-86 AC 5 as fully satisfied on that basis — say which half you have.

### Deletion that is legitimate: retention jobs

`ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS_v1.3.md:94-106` gives provisional per-category values (work time ≥ 2 years, planning history 3 years, pure sickness status ≤ 12 months after year end, audit 3 years, security logs 90 days, notifications 90 days, weather cache 48h–7d). `local_date` is what makes these queryable and indexable. Two caveats that must not be glossed: the table is explicitly "noch rechtlich zu prüfen" (`:92`), `PRD:154` makes legally reviewed retention a production gate, and `PRD:188` lists it as an open decision. EYT-86 therefore ships the **columns and indexes** that make retention implementable and ships **no deletion job** — building one now would encode unapproved legal values as executable behaviour.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Mitgliedschaftsoptionen (PostgreSQL 16+)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Nachtrag zu EYT-45. Die Tests oben pruefen `rolinherit` — ein Attribut der
-- ROLLE. Seit PostgreSQL 16 traegt aber die MITGLIEDSCHAFT eigene Flags, und
-- die entscheiden ueber das Verhalten von SET ROLE:
--
--   inherit_option = false  -> Rechte von authenticated werden NICHT automatisch
--                              vererbt; ohne `set local role` gibt es keine.
--   set_option     = true   -> `set local role authenticated` ist ueberhaupt
--                              erlaubt. Ohne dieses Flag koennte die Anwendung
--                              den Kontext gar nicht setzen und jede Fachquery
--                              schluege fehl.
--   admin_option   = false  -> easytree_app darf die Mitgliedschaft nicht
--                              weitergeben.
--
-- Ohne diese drei Zusicherungen waere die Rollenattribut-Pruefung oben allein
-- unvollstaendig: eine Mitgliedschaft mit abweichenden Optionen koennte das
-- Verhalten aendern, ohne dass `rolinherit` sich bewegt.
select is(
  (
    select m.inherit_option
    from pg_auth_members m
    join pg_roles member on member.oid = m.member
    join pg_roles grantor on grantor.oid = m.roleid
    where member.rolname = 'easytree_app' and grantor.rolname = 'authenticated'
  ),
  false,
  'Mitgliedschaft easytree_app -> authenticated vererbt NICHT automatisch (inherit_option)'
);

select is(
  (
    select m.set_option
    from pg_auth_members m
    join pg_roles member on member.oid = m.member
    join pg_roles grantor on grantor.oid = m.roleid
    where member.rolname = 'easytree_app' and grantor.rolname = 'authenticated'
  ),
  true,
  'easytree_app darf set role authenticated ausfuehren (set_option) — sonst kaeme die Anwendung nie an Rechte'
);

select is(
  (
    select m.admin_option
    from pg_auth_members m
    join pg_roles member on member.oid = m.member
    join pg_roles grantor on grantor.oid = m.roleid
    where member.rolname = 'easytree_app' and grantor.rolname = 'authenticated'

  false,
  'easytree_app darf die Mitgliedschaft nicht weitergeben (admin_option)'
);

);

Two things from a scope review that checked what I had **asserted** rather than **measured**. Both were right.

## 1. Role attribute ≠ membership option

The suite verified `rolinherit` — an attribute of the **role**. Since PostgreSQL 16 the **membership** carries its own flags, and those are what govern `SET ROLE`:

| flag | expected | why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inherit_option` | `false` | decides whether `authenticated`'s rights arrive automatically — the whole point of NOINHERIT |
| `set_option` | `true` | decides whether `set local role authenticated` is permitted at all. Without it the application could never reach any rights and every business query would fail |
| `admin_option` | `false` | decides whether the membership can be passed on |

A membership with different options could change the behaviour **without `rolinherit` moving**, so the previous assertions were incomplete.

Plus a non-vacuity check: if the catalogue join returns no row, all three become `is(NULL, …)` and go red for the wrong reason. The fourth assertion separates *"option wrong"* from *"membership gone"*.

## 2. My idempotency justification was unmeasured

Migration `0003`'s header justifies the idempotent role creation with *"`supabase db reset` rebuilds the database but leaves the roles standing"*.

**That was never measured.** What the `db-gates` run for `9c58155` actually shows:

Seeding globals from roles.sql...
Applying migration 20260727004500_0003_app_role.sql...   (×3: start, reset 1, reset 2)
```

So what is proven is that the migration is **repeatable**. It does *not* show which branch of the `do` block ran, and therefore does **not** prove the role survives a reset.
